teachings.title: Immune System: Identity and Boundaries
teachings.summary: Explore the immune system as the body's guardian of identity and master of discernment. This teaching invites reflection on boundaries, self-protection, and the profound journey of integrating exiled parts of the self.
teachings.bodyMarkdown:
### Opening

Your immune system is your body’s tireless guardian. It is a complex network of specialized cells, organs, and molecules that are constantly patrolling, working to distinguish “self” from “other.” Its fundamental task is discernment: knowing what belongs and what doesn't. This intricate system attacks what threatens, defends against what invades, and heals what has been damaged.

### Core Teaching

The physical function of your immune system mirrors your psychological relationship with boundaries and self-protection. Immune issues often invite us to examine profound questions about identity, boundaries, and our relationship with what we perceive as “other.” 

From a reflective perspective, autoimmune disorders can be seen as representing an ultimate crisis of identity, where we may have become so alienated from parts of ourselves that our body treats them as invaders. Chronic inflammation may point to an ongoing perceived threat that never resolves, while immune deficiency might speak to exhaustion from constantly defending or having given up the fight. When we are perpetually attacking or defending, or when we cannot integrate challenging experiences and instead must wall them off, our immune system may reflect these same patterns. The exhaustion of chronic immune activation often mirrors the exhaustion of living in perpetual psychological conflict.

### What to Notice

Notice where you might be holding onto patterns of attack and defense in your life. Are there areas where you feel constantly threatened or where you have built walls to protect yourself? Pay attention to any feelings of alienation from parts of yourself—qualities you may have judged as unacceptable or experiences you have walled off because they were too painful.

### Reflection

How might you shift from a stance of attack and defend to one of discernment and integration? Consider what parts of yourself you may have exiled or rejected. How can you begin to welcome these shadow aspects back into your wholeness? When we can see every difficulty as an invitation to grow rather than a threat to destroy, we open ourselves to deeper healing.

### Practice

Take a few moments to sit quietly and bring your awareness to your body. Imagine a gentle, healing light surrounding you, offering protection without the need for walls. As you breathe, invite any exiled or rejected parts of yourself to come forward into this light. Acknowledge them without judgment, offering them compassion and acceptance. Remind yourself that at the deepest level, you are one with all that exists, and there is nothing you need to attack or defend against.

### Source Note

This teaching is adapted from *Elevate Your Body To Love Booklet* (2026) by Susan Drury.

teachings.title: The Body as Messenger
teachings.summary: Explore how physical symptoms serve as messengers from below conscious awareness, communicating deeper truths. Learn how subconscious paradigms and the holographic nature of the body reflect our inner beliefs and relational experiences.
teachings.bodyMarkdown:
## Opening

We often navigate the world without fully grasping the hidden forces shaping our experiences. As Susan Drury shares, "We don’t know what we don’t know." It is a profound invitation to shift our perspective on our physical experiences. Instead of viewing the body as a machine that occasionally malfunctions, we are invited to see it as a wise and persistent communicator. When we begin to listen, we discover that the body is not betraying us; rather, it is speaking to us through the language of sensation and symptom, urging us to pay attention to what lies beneath our conscious awareness.

## Core Teaching

The core of this teaching invites us to reframe our relationship with physical discomfort and illness. Symptoms are not mere annoyances or signs of failure; they are messengers from the depths of our being. Pain is information. Chronic conditions act as persistent teachers, steadfastly refusing to be ignored until we are willing to investigate the deeper messages they carry. If we merely treat the symptoms without addressing the underlying causes, these messages often return or manifest in other ways, sometimes with even greater urgency.

This perspective is deeply intertwined with our early life experiences. As babies and children, we entered a complex world and instinctively formed belief systems about ourselves, others, and life itself. These belief systems, or paradigms, act as lenses through which we interpret reality, often defining the limits of our experiences and possibilities. Many of these paradigms operate from the hidden realm of the subconscious, silently orchestrating our experiences, relationships, and circumstances like a hidden puppeteer. When these paradigms restrict our ability to express our unique gifts and potential, the harmonious functioning of our body is also stifled, potentially resulting in physical symptoms. Treating these symptoms without considering the full context of our body, mind, emotions, and spirit only perpetuates the deeper conflicts being expressed.

Furthermore, the body is holographic in nature. This means that all our experiences, whether internal or external, are received and reflected not only mentally or emotionally but also physically. For instance, challenges in "digesting" certain life situations may manifest in the digestive system. The flexibility of our hips may mirror our flexibility in relationships. This holographic reality also implies that mindfully engaging with any part of our body can catalyze transformation throughout our entire system. Healing a physical tension, like in the shoulders, can shift how we carry responsibilities in our lives. True healing and transformation must embrace the entirety of our being: mind, emotions, spirit, and body as one interconnected system.

## What to Notice

Notice when you experience physical discomfort or recurring symptoms. Instead of immediately seeking to suppress or eliminate the sensation, pause and observe it with curiosity. Notice any accompanying emotions, thoughts, or life circumstances that arise simultaneously. Pay attention to areas where you feel "stuck" or restricted, both physically and in your daily life. Notice if there are patterns in how you respond to stress or challenges, and whether these patterns correspond to specific physical sensations. Be gentle with yourself as you observe, recognizing that the body is simply trying to communicate.

## Reflection

Consider a current or past physical symptom. If this symptom were a messenger, what might it be trying to tell you? Reflect on the paradigms or belief systems you may have formed early in life. How might these hidden beliefs be influencing your current experiences and physical well-being? Think about the holographic nature of your body. Are there areas in your life where you feel inflexible, burdened, or unable to "digest" experiences, and how might these be reflected in your physical body?

## Practice

The next time you notice a physical symptom or discomfort, take a few moments to sit quietly and bring your awareness to that area of your body. Breathe gently into the sensation without trying to change it. Ask your body, "What are you trying to tell me?" or "What do you need me to know?" Listen openly for any insights, images, or feelings that arise. You might find it helpful to journal about whatever comes up. Remember that this is a practice of building a compassionate and listening relationship with your body. If the sensations become overwhelming, give yourself permission to pause, ground yourself, and seek support if needed.

## Source Note

This teaching is adapted from "Elevate Your Body To Love Booklet" by Susan Drury, specifically the segment titled "The Body as Messenger."

teachings.title: Understanding Brain Frequencies
teachings.summary: Explore how different brain wave frequencies, such as beta and alpha, shape our daily awareness and perception. Learn how shifting into more receptive states can open the door to inspiration, creativity, and personal transformation.
teachings.bodyMarkdown:
### Opening

As we journey through our daily lives, our minds operate in various states of awareness, each shaped by specific energetic frequencies within our brains. Understanding these frequencies can offer profound insights into how we engage with the world, process stress, and access our deeper potential for creativity and transformation. By observing the subtle shifts in our consciousness, we can begin to intentionally cultivate states of mind that support our healing and growth.

### Core Teaching

Our human equipment includes a brain that operates within distinct energetic frequencies, commonly known as brain waves. These include beta, alpha, and theta states, each manifesting a unique range of perception and awareness. While different parts of our brain can simultaneously operate in various frequencies, our consciousness typically focuses predominantly on one at any given moment.

During our waking hours, as adults, we mostly reside in the beta frequency range. This state is outward-oriented, deeply engaged with the external world. It is the frequency of problem-solving, planning, brainstorming, and navigating the complexities of daily life. In its lower to mid ranges, beta is highly productive. However, when the frequency escalates into high beta, we often find ourselves in the stress zone—characterized by criticism, anxiety, and a tendency toward negative perceptions. In beta, our minds are busy "doing": remembering the past, worrying about the future, and feeling the pressure of immediate demands.

In contrast, when we begin to fall asleep, daydream, or enter a meditative state, our brains naturally shift into the alpha frequency. This state is less active and far more receptive. It allows us to move beyond the constraints of the beta paradigm, opening us to new discoveries, understandings, and solutions. The alpha state provides access to a wellspring of inspiration and creativity that the busy beta frequency simply does not have the bandwidth to realize. It is within this alpha state that we can consciously harness our brain's innate ability to facilitate our own change and transformation.

### What to Notice

Pay attention to the moments in your day when your mind feels busy, pressured, or anxious. These are often signs that you are operating in high beta. Notice how your body responds to this state—perhaps with tension, shallow breathing, or a sense of urgency. Conversely, observe the moments when you feel relaxed, open, or creatively inspired. These are glimpses of the alpha state. Recognizing these shifts is the first step toward consciously navigating your internal landscape.

### Reflection

Consider how often you find yourself in the "doing" mode of the beta frequency versus the "being" mode of the alpha frequency. How does the stress of high beta impact your perception of yourself and others? What small changes could you make to invite more alpha-state moments into your daily routine, allowing for greater receptivity and inspiration?

### Practice

Find a quiet space where you can sit comfortably without interruption. Close your eyes and take several deep, slow breaths, allowing your body to relax with each exhale. Consciously invite your mind to shift from the busy beta state to a more receptive alpha state. You might visualize a gentle wave washing over you, carrying away the need to solve problems or plan for the future. Spend a few minutes simply resting in this open, creative space, noticing any new thoughts or feelings that arise without judgment or attachment.

### Source Note

This teaching is grounded in the foundational concepts explored in Susan Drury's *Elevating Your Origins to Love: A Guided Journey of Transformation, Healing, and Power*, specifically focusing on the understanding of brain frequencies and their role in our awareness and transformation.

teachings.practiceInvitation: Take a few moments each day to consciously transition from the active beta state to the receptive alpha state. Through simple practices like deep breathing, daydreaming, or quiet meditation, invite your mind to rest and open up to new possibilities and inspiration.

teachings.title: Understanding Brain Frequencies
teachings.summary: Our daily experience of the world and our emotional well-being are deeply connected to the electrical rhythms of our brain. By understanding the five distinct categories of brainwaves, we can learn how different states of consciousness support healing, creativity, and spiritual emergence.
teachings.bodyMarkdown:
## Opening

The electrical activity emanating from our brain takes the form of brainwaves, which profoundly influence how we experience the world. There is an inseparable connection between our brainwave profile and our daily lives. When our brainwaves fall out of coherence, we may notice corresponding shifts in our emotional or physical well-being. By exploring the five categories of brainwaves—ranging from the most to the least active—we can better understand our own mental states and how they relate to healing, deep rest, and expanded awareness.

## Core Teaching

Our brain operates across a spectrum of frequencies, each supporting different aspects of our human experience. At the most active end are Gamma brainwaves (32–100 Hz). Once dismissed as mere "spare brain noise," Gamma is now recognized as the frequency of heightened perception and peak mental states. It is highly active during moments of universal love, altruism, and the expression of higher virtues. Because Gamma frequencies operate above the typical rate of neuronal firing, they remain somewhat mysterious, though they are often associated with expanded consciousness and spiritual emergence, and are regularly observed in long-term meditators.

Moving down the spectrum, we encounter Beta waves (13–30 Hz), the hallmark of a strongly engaged and aroused mind. When we are actively conversing, teaching, or figuring something out, we are in Beta. While essential for complex thought and integration, continual high-frequency Beta processing requires a tremendous amount of energy and can sometimes be associated with stress or high arousal.

Alpha waves (7.5–14 Hz) offer a shift into deep relaxation. This is the resting state of the brain, the "power of now" that emerges during daydreaming or light meditation. Alpha serves as a gateway to the subconscious, heightening imagination and aiding overall mental calmness and mind/body integration.

Deeper still is the Theta frequency (4–7.5 Hz), the realm of deep meditation, light sleep, and vivid dreams. In Theta, the constant chatter of the conscious mind quiets into a silent voice, making space for profound creativity, exceptional insight, and a deep spiritual connection with the universe. It is at the delicate border between Alpha and Theta where the optimal state for conscious creation and visualization begins.

Finally, Delta waves (0.5–4 Hz) represent the slowest frequencies, occurring during dreamless sleep and transcendental meditation. Delta is the gateway to the unconscious mind and the collective unconscious. This deep state of rest is vital, as it aids in the body's essential healing and regeneration processes.

## What to Notice

We are always projecting an energy field that extends beyond our physical bodies, and our brainwave states contribute to this emission. While we might not often think of ourselves in terms of energy, we regularly sense the "vibes" of others. Notice how your own energy feels throughout the day. Are you resting in the calm integration of Alpha, or are you running the high-energy, fast-idle engine of Beta? Recognizing these subtle shifts can offer insight into your current state of coherence and well-being.

## Reflection

Consider how your daily routines might be supporting or hindering the natural fluctuation of your brainwaves. Are you allowing yourself the quiet space needed to slip into the restorative states of Alpha and Theta, or are you predominantly operating in the high-demand state of Beta? Reflect on how your internal rhythm might be influencing the energy field you project into the world and how it impacts those around you.

## Practice

I invite you to create a small window of transition in your day to consciously invite a slower brainwave state. Find a quiet, comfortable place to sit and gently close your eyes. Allow your focus to rest lightly on your breath, noticing the simple rise and fall of your chest. As you breathe, consciously give yourself permission to step away from the active engagement of your day. Visualize your mental activity softening, like a fast-moving stream gently widening into a calm, still pool. Rest in this quiet space for a few minutes, simply being present with whatever arises, and notice if you feel a subtle shift in your energy or a deepened sense of calm before you return to your daily activities.

## Source Note

This teaching is derived from *Elevating Your Origins to Love: A Guided Journey of Transformation, Healing, and Power* (pages 253–256).

teachings.title: Nervous System: Safety and Connection
teachings.summary: Your nervous system is a vast communication network constantly monitoring for safety and connection. By recognizing how past experiences shape your responses, you can consciously rewire these pathways toward relaxation and trust.
teachings.bodyMarkdown:
### Opening

The nervous system is the fastest communication network in your body—a vast, lightning-like web of electrical signals that constantly monitors your inner and outer environment. It is always asking a fundamental question: "Am I safe?" This intricate system operates largely below conscious awareness, making split-second decisions based not only on your present circumstances but on the accumulated data of your past experiences. It is the physical manifestation of your relationship with safety, connection, and trust, guiding how you move through the world and interact with the people around you.

### Core Teaching

Our nervous systems are beautifully designed to protect us, assessing safety or danger and directing our responses accordingly. However, the issues we experience in our nervous system often examine fundamental questions of worthiness and whether we can trust life enough to relax into it. When we experience chronic pain, numbness, anxiety, or an inability to "settle down," these may point to a nervous system that has learned the world is not safe. It may have internalized a belief that pursuing authentic desires brings punishment, or that you must remain vigilantly on guard simply to survive.

The deeper pattern almost always traces back to childhood, a time when neural pathways were being laid down during years of genuine dependence on others for survival. If your early environment was unpredictable, critical, or dangerous—or if expressing your true feelings brought ridicule or punishment—your nervous system wired itself accordingly to protect you. These early-formed pathways can become default routes for the rest of your life unless you consciously intervene. You may remain "nervous," unable to fully relax even when your present circumstances are objectively safe, because your nervous system is still responding to programs formed decades ago. The profound invitation here is to realize that these patterns are not permanent; they are learned responses that can be gently and compassionately unlearned.

### What to Notice

Notice the moments when your body feels unable to settle, even in a safe environment. Pay attention to feelings of hypervigilance, anxiety, or the subtle expectation of danger or criticism. Observe how your physical body responds to rest—is there a resistance to relaxing, or a sudden spike in nervous energy when you try to be still? These are not flaws, but the echoes of ancient protective pathways doing exactly what they were trained to do. Frame these observations not as diagnoses, but as symbolic reflections of where your body is asking for reassurance and a renewed sense of safety. Notice the specific situations, environments, or interactions that trigger these old pathways, and meet them with curiosity rather than judgment.

### Reflection

Consider how your early environments may have shaped your current expectations of safety and danger. In what areas of your life do you feel you must remain on guard to survive? How might your physical inability to relax be connected to old beliefs about worthiness and the safety of expressing your authentic self? Reflect on what it might feel like to trust your environment and yourself enough to let down your guard, even just a little bit at a time.

### Practice

Recognize that you have the profound ability to rewire these ancient pathways. You are no longer the powerless child who needs hypervigilance to survive. Begin to consciously create new neural pathways by repeatedly choosing to envision safety, rather than automatically expecting danger. Seek gentle practices that help guide your nervous system into relaxation. Flex your muscles of courage, even when it still feels a little scary, to step into a new way of being. When you release a worldview based on danger, your nervous system empowers a different reality—one where you can live in safety, appreciation, acceptance, and joy.

### Source Note

This teaching is derived from the "Elevate Your Body To Love Booklet" by Susan Drury, focusing on the nervous system and its connection to safety, trust, and the rewiring of old patterns. Please remember that this exploration is for personal reflection and growth. Always consult with a qualified healthcare professional for medical advice, diagnosis, or treatment regarding nervous system health or any physical symptoms.

teachings.title: Reproductive System: Creation and Sexuality
teachings.summary: Explore the reproductive system as the sacred portal of creation, governing not just biological reproduction but all creative endeavors and life force energy. Reflect on the deeper patterns of shame or disconnection that may affect this system, and discover the invitation to reclaim your generative power and sexuality as divine gifts.
teachings.bodyMarkdown:
## Opening

Your reproductive system is the sacred center of creation itself. It is the biological expression of your capacity to bring forth new life, encompassing not just children, but all creative endeavors. This system operates through an exquisite hormonal orchestration, governing fertility, desire, passion, and fundamental life force energy. Even beyond its procreative function, it represents your primal power, your creative essence, and your connection to the eternal cycle of birth, death, and renewal.

## Core Teaching

The reproductive system serves as a powerful symbol of our generative capabilities. It is the seat of our creative power, whether that manifests as bringing new life into the world, birthing a new project, or cultivating passion in our daily lives. However, many of us carry deep wounds around sexuality, creativity, shame, and our fundamental right to generate new life in any form. 

Issues such as infertility, painful cycles, hormonal imbalances, or sexual dysfunction may point to a feeling of being disengaged. We might find ourselves disconnected from the cyclical nature of creative energies, or feeling ashamed of our sexuality and desires. These challenges often reflect ancestral, collective, or cultural wounds that have held this generative power as dangerous or shameful. For centuries, cultural and religious conditioning has frequently separated the erotic from the sacred, particularly demonizing female sexuality. This creates a profound split, where the very center of our creative power becomes the repository of our deepest shame. When we cannot safely open, receive, and express our most vulnerable, intimate selves, our reproductive system may manifest this closure through pain, dysfunction, and an inability to create.

## What to Notice

Notice the ways in which you relate to your own creative power and sexuality. Are there areas where you feel closed off, ashamed, or disconnected? Pay attention to any physical symptoms or discomfort in your reproductive center, viewing them not as mere biological failures, but as invitations to explore deeper emotional or energetic blockages. Observe the stories you tell yourself about pleasure, desire, and your right to create.

## Reflection

Consider the impact of cultural or ancestral conditioning on your relationship with your reproductive system. How might old narratives of shame or danger be influencing your current capacity for joy, intimacy, and creation? Reflect on what it might mean to heal this split, to reunite the sacred with the erotic, and to reclaim your body as a vessel of divine generative power.

## Practice

Begin to reclaim your body as the sacred vessel of creation and pleasure that it is. Honor your sexuality and creative power as divine, dynamic gifts rather than shameful burdens. Recognize that pleasure is your birthright, and that your capacity to create is holy. When you embrace your sexuality with joy and authenticity, and when you recognize your reproductive center as a sacred portal, you reclaim a fundamental truth: you are a creator, and your generative power is a blessing to yourself and all of life.

## Source Note

This teaching is drawn from Susan Drury's *Elevate Your Body To Love Booklet*, exploring the profound connection between our physical reproductive systems and our broader creative and sexual energies.

teachings.title: Stomach: Metabolizing Experience
teachings.summary: The stomach serves as an alchemical cauldron, not just for physical food, but for our life experiences. By exploring the symbolic connection between our digestion and our capacity to process life's challenges, we can transform difficult circumstances into wisdom.
teachings.bodyMarkdown:
### Opening
Your stomach begins the transformation of external sustenance into life force through an acidic crucible. This physical process of breaking down food mirrors your psychological capacity to metabolize life's experiences. When life feels "too much to stomach," or relationships leave a "sour taste," your stomach becomes the physical embodiment of these energetic realities.

### Core Teaching
Just as your stomach discerns what to break down and what to reject as toxic, you constantly choose what experiences to digest and what to eliminate. When you carry an overly acidic perspective—feeling burned by betrayal or embittered by experiences—your stomach reflects this internal state. The physical symptoms you may experience, such as indigestion, are your body's way of expressing that something on a deeper level is making you sick.

The acid meant to dissolve food into nourishment turns corrosive when your inner perspective on life becomes caustic. What you have not been able to "stomach" in your relationships, circumstances, and self-image accumulates as unprocessed experience that your stomach must contend with.

### What to Notice
Pay attention to moments when you feel "burned" by something or when an experience leaves a "sour taste." Notice how your stomach feels in these moments. Is it tight? Acidic? These physical sensations are valuable indicators of your energetic and emotional state.

### Reflection
Consider what experiences or relationships you are currently finding difficult to digest. Are there aspects of your life that you are rejecting rather than metabolizing? How might shifting your perspective from recoiling to receiving change your internal state?

### Practice
Can you develop a palate for life's full spectrum of flavors? Can you trust that challenging experiences contain nutrients for your evolution? Practice becoming a masterful alchemist, consciously choosing to transform difficult circumstances into wisdom and strength. When you shift from burning to metabolizing, your stomach returns to its sacred work of nourishing you with everything life offers.

### Source Note
Adapted from Susan Drury's "Elevate Your Body To Love Booklet," page 37.

teachings.title: Head: Consciousness and Identity
teachings.summary: Explore the head as the crown of consciousness and the throne of identity. Learn how physical symptoms in the head can reflect a conflict between mental control and intuitive flow, and discover how to relax into higher guidance.
teachings.bodyMarkdown:
## Opening

Your head is the physical home of your brain, a complex universe that shapes your experience of being "you." Over time, your experiences carve neural pathways—grooves through which your consciousness habitually flows. Often, these patterns create a sense of identity that you might mistakenly believe is the entirety of who you are. The head serves as both the command center for survival and the seat of the ego, frequently narrating a story of separation, fear, and a need for control.

## Core Teaching

When we look closely at the head, we see it as a space where consciousness and identity intersect. The deeper pattern often involves a disconnection from our inner guidance. When we listen too much to external voices and ignore the "still, small voice within," we create tension. Accumulating knowledge purely for protection, judging ourselves harshly based on internalized criticism, or pressuring ourselves to meet impossible standards turns the head into a battlefield. Here, fear and love, ego and soul, wage an ongoing struggle. The discomfort or pain we feel can be understood as consciousness literally pressing against the constraints of limited belief systems.

## What to Notice

Issues in the head often reveal a conflict between intellectual knowledge and heart wisdom, or between the desire for mental control and the natural flow of intuition. Physical symptoms like headaches, migraines, or head injuries may correlate with overthinking, the pressure to figure everything out mentally, or the strain of trying to perform or present yourself as someone other than who you truly are. *Note: These symbolic associations are offered as reflective possibilities rather than medical diagnoses or causes. Please consult a qualified healthcare professional for any physical symptoms or treatment decisions.*

## Reflection

Consider how much pressure you place on yourself to understand everything intellectually. Are there areas in your life where you are trying to force a mental solution rather than allowing your intuition to guide you? Notice if you are holding onto internalized criticism or impossible standards that create tension in your mind and body.

## Practice

Begin to release the mental gymnastics of trying to figure everything out. Trust that you are completely capable and equipped with a wisdom that goes beyond intellectual understanding. While your brain is a magnificent tool, it is not meant to be the sole authority on how you live your life. Cultivate a relationship with your intuition, the wisdom of your body, and the knowing of your heart. Accept yourself as enough, exactly as you are. As you practice trusting higher guidance, notice how your head can relax into its true purpose: serving as the crown of consciousness through which divine intelligence expresses itself.

## Source Note

Adapted from Susan Drury's *Elevate Your Body To Love Booklet*, page 26.

teachings.title: Lungs: Life-Force Exchange
teachings.summary: Explore the lungs as the intimate interface between your inner world and the external atmosphere. This teaching invites you to reflect on how you draw in vital life energy and consciously release what is no longer needed.
teachings.bodyMarkdown:
### Opening

The respiratory system serves as an intimate and profound interface between your inner world and the vast external atmosphere. It represents a continuous, sacred exchange that reveals how you engage with life itself. Each breath you take is a powerful act: drawing in vital life energy and releasing what is toxic or no longer needed. The lungs are unique in that they are the only internal organs in constant contact with the external world, making them a powerful symbol of our relationship with our environment and our capacity to fully embrace the gift of life.

### Core Teaching

Breath operates both automatically and consciously, revealing your innate power to shift from a passive participant to a conscious creator of your own experience. When we look at the lungs, we see the profound physiological and symbolic purpose of the sacred exchange of life force. You deserve to inflate the full gift of your life, to draw in inspiration completely, and to release whatever is not yours to carry.

Respiratory patterns often point to conflicts around how much life-supporting breath you can take in, and what you feel you cannot release. Depression and anxiety can sometimes manifest as shallow breathing, reflecting a feeling of being unable to fully inspire an enlivened existence. Chronic conditions may speak to feeling suffocated by circumstances, unable to exhale toxic elements, or having something embedded so deeply that it compresses vitality yet feels impossible to expel.

### What to Notice

Notice how you breathe when you feel overwhelmed by circumstances or when grief clouds your joy. Pay attention to whether your breathing is shallow or deep, and whether you feel you can fully inhale and exhale. Reflect on whether there are toxic elements or deep-seated issues that feel difficult to release. These symbolic associations are offered as reflective possibilities rather than causes or diagnoses. If you are experiencing physical symptoms or need guidance on treatment decisions, please seek qualified medical care.

### Reflection

Consider what inspirations you are willing to accept into your life. What are you choosing to release, and what obstructions do you believe are too embedded to fully "exhale" from your life? How can you recreate your environment to abundantly provide everything you need to breathe freely and deeply?

### Practice

Take a moment to sit quietly and focus on your breath. With each inhale, imagine drawing in vital life energy, inspiration, and joy. With each exhale, consciously release whatever is not yours to carry, along with any perceived limitations or toxic elements. Allow yourself to fully expand into joyful aliveness, giving yourself permission to recreate an environment that supports your well-being.

### Source Note

This teaching is a faithful adaptation grounded in Susan Drury's *Elevate Your Body To Love Booklet*, exploring the physiological and symbolic purpose of the lungs and the sacred exchange of life force.

teachings.title: Questioning What We Know
teachings.summary: Explore the practice of suspending what you "know" to create space for deeper wisdom. This guided meditation invites you to gently examine the beliefs and assumptions you hold as absolute truth, observing how they impact your relationships and self-concept.
teachings.bodyMarkdown:
## Opening

*Not knowing is true knowledge.*
*Presuming to know is a disease.*
*First realize that you are sick;*
*Then you can move towards health.*

As you prepare yourself for this exploration, consider this verse from the *Tao Te Ching*. For the moment, stand the idea of "knowing" something right on its head. Suspend—just for a moment—your knowings and see what that's like.

## Core Teaching

When you have some quiet time and space, sit comfortably and close your eyes. You may have lots of thoughts in your mind right now. Reading this may have triggered some memories or questions, so it may take a little time for them to settle down.

As we have done before, an easy way to focus yourself and disengage from random thoughts is to pay attention to your breath. To your breathing. To the in of the inhale. To the out of the exhale.

Notice where the breath goes as you inhale. How deeply does it move into your body? How long is it? How does it feel? What is the quality of your breath? And the exhale—what is it like? How long is it?

Keeping your full attention on your breath, invite the inhale to move more deeply into your body. You don't necessarily need to increase the length of time of the inhale, but gently invite it in more deeply. And at the same time, slightly increase the length of your exhale.

Keep inviting the breath comfortably in a little deeper, and slightly increasing the length of your exhales. If you can, reach toward having your exhales be twice the length of your inhales—but if that's too much of a stretch, then just find a rhythm that's comfortable and stay with it, counting (if you like) the length of your inhales and then the exhales.

## What to Notice

Once you are feeling relaxed and focused, you can ask yourself if there is anything you would like to explore and shift, around the idea of knowing. Of wondering whether you know enough. Of being adequate in your knowing. Of knowing what is right and what is wrong. Of knowing something different about something you have assumed was true.

How do you relate to the need to know, in your life?

Notice what comes up. How you feel in your body when you question whether you know something or don't know something you think you should. Follow the sensations, the feelings, without judgment. Just observe and be present to them.

And now: What would it be like to not know?

For this moment, imagine you don't know. That you have a blank space. A beautiful emptiness.

Imagine that you don't need to know. That there is nothing you need to know. About yourself. About others.

If you are a person who has very strong opinions, who truly knows you know what's the absolute right way to do or be—or how the world should be—this may feel confrontational. What do you mean, I don't know? Try not to get too affronted here; it's just an exploration, you can return to all your knowings in a few minutes. No one is saying that you don't know; there is nothing to defend against here.

## Reflection

Just experiment, for a few minutes, with what it's like not to know. And not to need to know.

Imagine all the knowings that have been crowded into your mind over the course of your lifetime. Do any images come to you? Just be present to them.

Imagine all the knowings you constantly try to secure—how something should be done. How a situation should turn out. All the lessons, all the dictates, all the shoulds and shouldn'ts, all the beliefs you have, all the book learnings and newspaper articles and absorbed understandings, all the rules and laws and customs, all the many knowings that you have acquired and come to believe as truth that pertains to you… to others… to societies… to countries… governments… organizations… partnerships… parents and children… siblings…

The amount of knowing within your brain is huge!

Get a sense of these knowings. How do they feel to you? Are they heavy or light? Joyful or burdensome? Are some knowings more important to you than others? Are some absolutely sacrosanct, so that to even question them feels like blasphemy?

Just notice. Don't judge anything you are experiencing, simply become aware. Become aware of how it feels within you to have all these knowings.

Do some of them feel different than others? Are some of them more natural or do some of them feel restrictive? Do any of them seem to focus or be held in a particular part of your body?

Notice if there are any individual knowings that you feel are really and truly TRUE. That you hold as gospel.

Take one out from the pile and look at it. How do you feel about this knowing? About what you know about the knowing? Do you have any judgments about this knowing? How does it contribute to your experience in life? How does it affect your relationship with others? How does it affect your self-concept? How does it affect your work—or your leisure time?

## Practice

Ask yourself how this knowing impacts your relationships with other people. Does it ever separate you from others? Cause you to hold others as wrong? Or superior? Does it ever make you feel wrong? Or put any kind of barrier between you and them?

Just look at this; don't get too involved, other than sitting in the question and seeing what you notice.

For fun—and this is strictly for fun, you don't have to do it if you don't want to—imagine one of the knowings you feel quite attached to, doesn't exist. That you don't know anything about it.

That you have absolutely no opinion on this subject at all. That you feel completely neutral toward the whole thing. That there is no judgment one way or another within you, on this.

Take some time here. It can seem impossible, so don't push yourself to where you can't go—but just imagine IF. IF you didn't even know this at all. IF you had no opinion or even awareness about it.

What would it change for you? How would it affect your life, your experience, and your relationships? How would it affect how you saw others, or what you expected of them? How would it affect what you expected of yourself?

Not knowing is true knowing; presuming to know is a disease. Imagine if you simply erased your knowing, and it no longer took up any space within you. How would you feel? How would it change your life?

Just for fun, notice if certain aspects of your life would feel better. Or freer.

Are there ways that this knowing has actually hampered or constricted you in any way? Not that we want you to go out and start robbing banks or shooting people you don't like—clearly this isn't about anarchy or breaking necessary laws—but it IS about questioning those knowings that restrict or limit you. That restrain your fulfilment or free expression. That tarnish your appreciation of yourself or others. That keep you from experiencing more of life's goodness and satisfaction.

Has your knowing placed a restraint over your ability to fully flow with life? With yourself? With others? Has your knowing caused you to criticize or condemn things that you would actually rather feel a sense of peace around?

The lines of the verse say, "first realize you are sick—then you can move towards health." Perhaps there are some knowings that you absorbed from long ago that no longer serve your highest good. That no longer serve the highest good of others, or even of the world. What would it feel like to live free of that yoke of knowing? Free of opinions that straitjacket you and keep you from your own deeper wisdom?

Sit in the imagination of it.

Allow yourself to vibrate to a frequency where that knowing is no longer influencing you. Find a frequency free of that restriction, where you create a different kind of experience. To not know. To just explore, to experiment. To accept others in their freedom. To accept yourself as already whole.

Sit with this as long as you are comfortable. When you start getting distracted or need to return to your outer life, see if you can bring an aspect of this new awareness with you.

If there are some old knowings you want to keep dismantled, be on the lookout. When you notice yourself falling back into that old pattern of knowing, catch yourself—and then deliberately disengage from it. Often it will be so automatic, you won't notice until you are quite far down the path of the belief; but bit by bit, you will get faster at recognizing it, faster at deconstructing your automatic responses and eventually realize you have a new openness to life. To others. To yourself.

## Source Note

*Lao-Tzu, trans. Stephen Mitchell, "Chapter 71," in Tao Te Ching: A New English Version (New York, NY: HarperPerennial, 1988).* This teaching is derived from *Elevating Your Origins to Love* by Susan Drury.

teachings.title: Tuning Into Your Nervous System
teachings.summary: Explore the automatic wiring of your nervous system and how it responds to stress. By observing your physical sensations, emotions, and thoughts without judgment, you can begin to guide your neural pathways toward a state of relaxation, connection, and self-mastery.
teachings.bodyMarkdown:
## Opening

When we consider the physical manifestations of energy, our separateness seems undeniable. We each have our own distinct experiences and perspectives. But what causes us to experience this differentiation? It appears to be our physiological equipment—especially our brain and nervous system—that translates the various energies in and around us, giving rise to the specific details of our world. To understand how we perceive reality through our nervous system, we can turn our attention inward and explore our direct experience.

## Core Teaching

Our nervous system is an automatic wiring system that is constantly active, processing our experiences and generating reactions. Whether we are in a genuinely threatening situation or simply thinking about a stressful event, our brain and body work in concert to produce a cascade of physiological, chemical, neurological, and hormonal processes. These processes affect our body, mind, and emotions, all of which contribute to our overall energy field.

The three primary reactions of a stress-activated nervous system are fight, flight, and freeze. The "fight" response is characterized by an aggressive, hot sensation, a feeling that others are against us, and an impulse to rise up and defend ourselves. The "flight" response is akin to a prey animal bursting into motion to escape a predator, a strong desire to get away from the situation. The "freeze" response is like a deer caught in headlights, so overwhelmed by fear that it becomes immobilized, unable to speak, think, or move.

When we are in the grip of a stress or defensive response, we often feel isolated. There is little sense of safety, relaxation, or community. This alienating state consumes our resources and energy to mount a defense. However, our optimal human blueprint is designed to return to a state of relaxation, rejuvenation, reconnection, and restoration once the threat has passed. In this restorative state, our bodies can repair and rest, and we can re-engage with activities that inspire us and connect with others.

## What to Notice

As you begin to explore your nervous system, notice the ever-changing inner landscape of your body, emotions, and mind. Observe the sensations that arise when you think of a stressful situation—perhaps a tightening in your stomach, chest, shoulders, neck, or head. Notice any emotions that accompany these physical sensations, such as fear, anger, panic, or frustration. Pay attention to the thoughts running through your mind, particularly those that focus on what is wrong with the situation.

It is also important to notice how your energy shifts during these automatic stress reactions. How would you describe your energy in those moments? What effect does that energy have on your body, your perception of yourself, and your feelings toward others? By making these previously unconscious processes conscious, you can begin to observe and feel what is happening on multiple levels whenever you become activated.

## Reflection

Reflect on your personal stress cycle and how your nervous system responds to activation. Can you identify which of the three main stress responses—fight, flight, or freeze—you tend to experience most frequently? 

Consider your ability to return to a state of well-being after a stressful event. Do you have a healthy, automatic ability to return to rest, relaxation, and connection? Or do you find that you remain on alert even after recognizing that there is no immediate threat? If you struggle to feel safe or at ease, it may indicate that you have developed strong neural pathways associated with the fight, flight, or freeze responses. Recognizing this is a valuable step, as it reveals potentials within you that are ripe for retuning to create a more satisfying life experience.

## Practice

Sit quietly in a place free from distractions, ensuring you do not need to be alert to the external world. Think of a stressful situation you are currently facing. Close your eyes and turn your attention inward to your body. Observe any physical sensations, noting their location, quality, and density. Do they remain static or change? Tune into any emotions present and ask yourself what the physical sensation of that emotion feels like. Remain an observant detective of your inner experience without trying to change or suppress anything. Notice any reactions to your own physical or emotional responses. Ask yourself: How safe do I feel right now? How comfortable am I in my body? How connected do I feel to others? Allow your body to move, shift, or stretch if it desires, remaining keenly present to any changes. Finally, let the image of the stressful situation fade, bringing yourself back to the present moment. Take a few slow, deep breaths, open your eyes, and find something soothing to look at, noticing any further internal relaxation.

## Source Note

This teaching is derived from Susan Drury's exploration of the nervous system and its role in translating energy into our lived experience. It emphasizes the importance of conscious observation and self-mastery in guiding our neural pathways toward greater well-being.

teachings.title: Feeling Joy
teachings.summary: This teaching invites you to deliberately cultivate a feeling of joy, even in the midst of life's challenges. Through a guided practice of sensory recall, you are encouraged to connect with your original essence and balance the sufferings of the world with regular forays into joy.
teachings.bodyMarkdown:
### Opening

Somewhere underneath, despite our movements, exposures, and experiences, despite the people, situations, and crises, we still have access to joy, excitement, anticipation, and buoyancy. We may have lost awareness of them; we may have become so affected by the hurts and wrongs of human life that we are influenced away from them, and yet they remain.

It may seem superficial or even irresponsible to deliberately seek a feeling of joy in a world full of suffering. It may seem to invalidate our own suffering, or that of others, to consciously tune away from the wrongs and nurture a spark of joy within us. And yet, by remaining aligned with all the hurts and wrongs and traumas we have lived, we stay stuck perpetuating them within our own energy system. We breed further resentment and anger and hatred and fear — for ourselves, and for others.

How about experimenting a little? How about giving your system a chance to experience, even if just for a moment, what has never stopped being available within you. The feeling of joy.

### Core Teaching

When we focus our attention on something, we are potentiating it. We make it more available to our experience. Begin to explore choosing how you want to feel. Begin to return your own awareness to that original reality: the joy of simply being alive.

For our own well-being and that of others, we should try to balance the sufferings of the world with regular forays into joy. Into peace. Into contentment. Because just as surely as we came into the world, we will one day leave it — and all the possibilities we could have lived, all the joy and enlivenment we could have felt, all the appreciation we could have offered to ourselves and others in our lifetime, will no longer be there.

### What to Notice

How easy was this for you to do? If it was difficult, then consider whether you have become used to looking for what’s wrong in life, rather than appreciating what’s right.

Notice if you feel resistance. It’s a courageous act to reach for joy in the midst of a world that focuses so much attention on what’s wrong. If we listen to the news at night, feeling joy can almost seem irresponsible.

Does your mind have a different opinion on this? Does it feel you shouldn’t be doing this? You can watch your mind but stay disengaged from the thoughts. Focus on keeping your energy untouched by anything other than joy.

### Reflection

Take time to reflect on your relationship with joy. Are you allowing yourself to feel it fully, or do you hold back out of guilt or fear? How might your life change if you made joy a regular practice, rather than an occasional accident?

Consider the moments in your life when joy flowed effortlessly. What conditions were present? How can you recreate those conditions internally, even when external circumstances are challenging?

### Practice

Sit quietly and think for a moment, looking through your life for a time when you felt joy. It was likely inspired by something — a beloved pet for example, or a perfect moment with someone you loved, or an experience in nature or listening to a particular piece of music. You will find something — perhaps many things! Pick one and go to that moment in your mind.

Close your eyes and see that moment. Where were you? Who were you with? What was around you? Get very specific in seeing the details of that moment. Bring it into full color.

Notice other aspects of the moment. Was there a particular fragrance in the air? A feeling of something on your skin? Were you eating something delicious or touching something wonderful? What sounds were there in the background?

Immerse yourself more and more, using all of your senses, into that experience. Continue to fill it out for yourself in as many dimensions as possible. Notice what you are feeling in your body right now, as you move back into that moment. How does it feel inside? Take your time and really focus on the physical sensations within you as you return to that experience.

And now — deliberately fill your heart with joy. Open yourself completely to the feeling, the emotion, of joy. Place all your attention there and remain fully focused on this feeling as you remain within the memory of that experience. This may take some attention; we aren’t used to deliberately creating a feeling — a positive feeling — for ourselves, so don’t be surprised if this is challenging. But keep going, keep opening yourself to the feeling of joy.

Now let the other aspects of the moment fade, and just keep your attention on the feeling of joy. Joy for its own sake. Joy for the hell of it. Joy because you can! Stay with it, stretching it out… Stay with joy… Stay with joy…

Stay loyal to joy. Feel it radiating from your heart, your gut. Feel it moving throughout your body. Feel it expanding beyond you, into the world. Feel joy permeating your original essence, your original energy. Know joy. Be joy. Embody joy.

### Source Note

Adapted from *Elevating Your Origins to Love: A Guided Journey of Transformation, Healing, and Power* by Susan Drury (2023).

In what ways might balancing the world's suffering with your own regular forays into joy benefit both you and those around you?

Immerse yourself in the sensory details of that memory—the sights, sounds, smells, and physical sensations. Once you feel the joy arising, let the details of the memory fade and focus solely on the feeling of joy itself, allowing it to radiate from your heart and permeate your entire body.

teachings.title: Discovering Space
teachings.summary: This guided practice invites you to shift from your busy beta mind into a more spacious alpha awareness through focused breathing. By observing the breath without trying to change it, you can begin to experience breath not as a thing, but as space-in-action. Ultimately, this practice offers a sense of being held by a vast, neutral space that connects all life.
teachings.bodyMarkdown:
## Opening

Can you imagine yourself before coming into this world? As pure energy, consciousness, or soul? This kind of imagining is difficult for our everyday, task-oriented "beta" brains. To explore wider possibilities, we are invited to be adventurous and bring our "alpha" minds forward—opening ourselves to something new.

## Core Teaching

When we turn our attention away from worldly concerns and thoughts, we create an opportunity to connect with a deeper sense of presence. The easiest way to begin this shift is by focusing on the breath. By simply observing the inhale and exhale without trying to change or alter anything, we step out of the need to "do" and into the experience of being.

As we deepen this focus, we may start to notice that breath isn't really a "thing" at all. It is more like space-in-action—space moving in, and space moving out. This space doesn't change whether it is inside or outside of your body. It stretches out, going beyond the room you are sitting in, beyond your immediate surroundings, and covering oceans and mountains.

Our planet itself is breathing space. All inhabitants—humans, animals, trees, oceans, mountains—are breathing. All the actions and interactions on the planet take place against this vast, neutral backdrop of breath and space. It is something that happens continually, automatically, and often unconsciously. This breath, this space, maintains our life. It holds us, serving as the cradle of our experiences and the neutral backdrop behind both our disappointments and triumphs. It simply IS.

## What to Notice

Notice the quality and rhythm of your breath. Where does it go in your body? What is its substance? As you focus, you may find your mind wandering to noises or thoughts. Notice this wandering without setting up an inner dialogue or judgment about it. Notice that breath is like space-in-action, and that this space is all around you, stretching out infinitely.

## Reflection

How would you describe your breath to someone else? Where does your breath come from, and where does it go? What does it feel like to consider that you are nurtured, held, and breathed by this vast space?

## Practice

Close your eyes and take some time to turn your attention away from worldly concerns. Focus on your breath, breathing in and out through your nose if possible. Simply observe the inhale and exhale without trying to change anything. Begin to count the length of your inhale, then your exhale, becoming absorbed in the counting for at least ten cycles. Then, release the counting and focus on the breath itself—feeling its quality and substance. If you get distracted, simply return your attention to your breath. Eventually, allow yourself to experience the breath as space—inside and outside your body. Feel yourself as simply Being Space, beyond your thoughts, achievements, or regrets. When you are ready, gently return to your outer world experience, noticing not just the "things" around you, but the space surrounding everything.

## Source Note

This teaching is adapted from *Elevating Your Origins to Love: A Guided Journey of Transformation, Healing, and Power* by Susan Drury.
keyThemes: Breath awareness
Alpha and beta mind states
Space and presence
Interconnectedness
Neutral observation
reflectionPrompts: How does your experience of your breath change when you view it as 'space-in-action' rather than just a physical function?
When you imagine the vast space that holds all life on the planet, how does that perspective affect your current worries or triumphs?
What challenges do you face when trying to maintain active attention on your breath, and how can you practice returning to it without self-judgment?
teachings.practiceInvitation: Set aside a few minutes today to practice this breath awareness. Find a quiet place, close your eyes, and follow the rhythm of your breath. Start by counting the length of your inhales and exhales for ten cycles, then transition to simply feeling the breath as space moving in and out. Allow yourself to rest in the feeling of being held by this expansive, neutral space.

teachings.title: The Calling of the Creative Force
teachings.summary: Revisit a pivotal, life-altering moment to recognize the deeper course of your destiny. Discover the creative principle that draws you forward through the seemingly random unfolding of your life.
teachings.bodyMarkdown:
### Opening

Sit quietly and think of a time when something truly and powerfully life-altering came forward; something that you hadn’t ever imagined happening. Perhaps meeting someone who went on to be important to you, discovering a place that you felt a strong connection to, or experiencing a seemingly unexpected happenstance that proved to be a pivotal moment in your life’s path. Take your time and allow something to come forward. There may be many moments, but pick one you would like to explore.

### Core Teaching

How these random moments add up is an equation we can never fully understand, and yet—there is a creative principle, a force that draws us always forward, always to the new, always ready and waiting underneath all our pregnant pauses. We are forever conceiving or gestating or delivering ourselves. 

We rarely have anything that’s pure bliss, but that’s not really to be expected when living in these forever-changing human bodies, in this forever-changing external world. We do our best growing within a variable spectrum of experiencing. So even if you notice portions of this future that didn’t work out, that met an unhappy end or that veered onto a totally different track, that’s okay. Rather than focus on how things didn’t work out, simply appreciate the parts of the journey where you clearly see how you did benefit, how you did grow, and how you discovered things about yourself that have remained important and meaningful.

### What to Notice

Notice all the things that had to happen for this moment to have come about. All the different paths that could have prevented you from being here, all the choices you had to make in order to meet this particular moment of destiny. Notice all that this moment began to usher forward into your life. Move forward in your mind’s eye and see the future it brought to you begin to unfold. Be aware of your emotions as you start to unpack the full destiny of that experience, as it slowly but surely opened up and blossomed in your life.

### Reflection

Consider that no matter how random life may seem, you are part of something vaster than what your mind alone may notice. See if you discover the path that, while meandering, has also been one of meaning and purpose through the many adventures and moments of your life. You might even recognize how those parts that didn’t work out opened a window for something important and powerful to come forward.

### Practice

Holding this pivotal moment in your mind, close your eyes. Turn your attention inward and travel back in your mind’s eye to that experience. Allow yourself to see it fully. Where were you? See the place. What colors do you notice? What are you doing? Feel the sensations in your body. What sounds might have been heard? Tune into the sounds of the experience, as they were happening in the moment. Are you with someone? Notice where they are in this moment. Go back further in your mind’s eye to all the preceding experiences, actions, or decisions that brought you to this pivotal moment. Live the moment, the meeting, the experience. Play it out once again in your mind’s eye. If you find yourself going down a painful cul-de-sac of feelings, breathe a little more deeply. Consciously and gently create a little more space within your body, within your psyche, to accommodate all the different facets that have made up your great life adventure—your hero’s journey—without negating any of them. Allow yourself to feel this deeper course, this deeper drawing of your own destiny or passage. Just sit with this for a few moments. In your own time, open your eyes. Look at something close to you. See it in its wholeness. It, too, has had its own journey and will continue its journey of change.

### Source Note

Derived from *Elevating Your Origins to Love: A Guided Journey of Transformation, Healing, and Power* by Susan Drury.
keyThemes: Destiny and Purpose
Creative Force
Life Transitions
Reflection and Awareness
Growth through Experience
reflectionPrompts: When you reflect on a pivotal moment in your life, what seemingly random choices or events had to align for it to occur?
How have the challenging or 'unsuccessful' parts of your journey opened windows for unexpected growth or new possibilities?
In what ways can you sense a deeper, creative force drawing you forward through the changing circumstances of your life?
teachings.practiceInvitation: Take time to sit quietly and vividly recall a pivotal moment in your life, engaging all your senses to reconstruct the experience. Trace the path of choices and events that led to this moment, and observe how it unfolded into your future. Breathe into any difficult emotions that arise, creating space to honor every facet of your journey without judgment.
sensitiveContentNotes: This practice involves revisiting past memories, which may evoke unexpected or difficult emotions. Please feel free to pause the practice or seek supportive care if you encounter overwhelming feelings or painful memories.

teachings.title: Creating a Foundation of Safety
teachings.summary: This practice guides you to establish a deep sense of physical and emotional safety by connecting with your breath and the earth. By gently soothing your nervous system and anchoring your awareness in your lower body, you can begin to rewire old patterns of fear and trepidation.
teachings.bodyMarkdown:
### Opening

Because bringing a new life into the world is never a sure thing; because your mother and father may have felt various measures of powerlessness in other areas of their lives; because the human experience offers a huge variety of threats and dangers, likely you were bathed in a certain amount of fear and trepidation about even coming into the world. Don't take it personally! The world can feel even scarier when you are growing a baby at the same time you are juggling all the other balls of your life in the air.

Let's assume you received a fair share—maybe even more than a fair share—of stress or anxiety messages while in the womb. And that your nervous system obediently wired itself along those lines, with neural pathways primed to sense danger and respond accordingly—even when the environment is actually benign and even welcoming. What to do about that?

### Core Teaching

Let's approach our inner workings from within, but instead of directly putting in mental messages, we're going to go to a different part of the body—the part of us that is most connected to the earth, to grounding, to stability, to security—and which is often where our first perceptions of danger are perceived, whether justified or not.

Sit comfortably—this exercise is better done sitting in a chair with your feet on the floor, rather than lying down—and once again, close your eyes. Turn your attention inward, away from the outer world with all its many distractions and activities, and instead notice your breath.

Discover that you are breathing! That in itself can be quite surprising! Amidst everything that is going on in your life, amidst all your busyness and doing, you have been continuing to breathe! And you didn't even have to think about it! It just happens, all by itself!

Tune into this whole breathing thing. Notice how you are breathing. How deep into your body does your breath go? How long are the inhales? The exhales? Take a few moments and just discover more intimately what your breathing is like.

*(If you have been breathing through your mouth, do your best to switch over to nose breathing. For some people this is hard, so if you feel you can't get enough air, then "sip" the breath in through just a corner of your mouth slowly and steadily. Try to exhale it through your nose. Over time, try to completely inhale through your nose, at least on every other breath. But only push yourself as far as is comfortable.)*

Now gradually invite the inhales a little deeper into your body. Don't force anything, just gently envision the breath going deeper, your lower ribcage expanding. And then a bit more deeply, expanding on the inhale, contracting as you exhale. Keep this gradual deepening of the breath going by gently, gently inhaling deeper into your body, into your lower abdomen.

As the breath moves in deeper, pay attention to your exhales. Gradually lengthen the exhales, extending them a bit further, releasing all of your breath.

If this is feeling difficult, if you are feeling any sense of anxiety or stress, here is a little variation called the straw breath. Continue to pursue these deeper inhales, but on the exhale, "blow" the breath out through your pursed lips—as though you were blowing through a straw. Blow out all the air this way, and then begin your next inhale. Keep this up for a minute or more until you notice you are feeling much more relaxed.

### What to Notice

Notice what you are feeling inside. You may eventually reach an inner state of calm.

Continuing to breathe in deeply, following with long, slow exhales, turn your attention to the bottom of your feet. Feel where they connect to the ground or floor beneath you.

Notice where the bottom of each toe meets the floor; where the soles of your feet meet the floor; the heels. Feel the sturdiness of the ground supporting your feet.

What does this feel like? Do you sense anything in your feet? Where they meet the ground? Imagine your feet spreading out on the ground, fully supported, fully rooted.

Our feet get so little attention. What does it feel like to focus completely on them, to bathe them in your attention? To appreciate how they connect you to the earth, how they allow you to walk upright and to move through the world?

Keeping your attention still peripherally on the bottoms of your feet and the ground, now begin to include the rest of your feet in your awareness. The sides and tops of your feet. Your ankles. Try not to lose awareness of where your feet are planted on the ground, as you expand your consciousness up; remain connected to the earth, even as you include more of your body in your perception.

### Reflection

Now move to include your lower legs. Your calves. Your knees. Keep checking back with the bottoms of your feet on the floor, as you expand upward. To your thighs. Your hips. Your pelvic floor.

And now just stay here, remaining very present to this whole lower part of your body—from your feet connected to the ground, up through your legs to your pelvic floor, hips, sacrum of your spine.

As you continue to be very aware of this part of your body, sit in these words: *I am safe. It is safe to be here.*

Notice if anything comes up. If so, don't resist, but instead be open to whatever feelings are coming up and embrace them within your awareness. Soothe them, allowing the words "I am safe. It is safe to be here" to continue resonating within you.

Keep your attention on this lower part of your body, continuing to sit in the resonance of the words, in the deep regularity of your breath.

*Safe.*
*Secure.*
*It is right that I am here.*
*I am welcome here.*
*I am safe here.*

If parts of you seem to come up in contradiction, don't be surprised. Not having a basic sense of safety is something many of us came in with. It probably goes back to your mother or father, or their mother or father, or to the ones before them.

### Practice

But now, sitting here in a safe, calm place, with your feet firmly planted on the floor, supported by the earth beneath you and the chair on which you sit, you can begin to cultivate a fuller sense of safety for yourself.

Let the words resonate in this lower part of your body. Feel them in the base of your spine.

What does that feel like? You may feel a sense of warmth or expansion. Or especially if your sense of safety is quite precarious, you may feel some unease. Or you may feel nothing at all.

Whatever your experience, try not to judge, try to not force something that doesn't yet feel true.

Just acknowledge you, like everyone else, is a work in progress.

Just because you are here, just because you managed to make it onto the planet and live the number of years you have lived, doesn't mean your nervous system isn't still kind of worried about this whole life thing … cut yourself some slack. You are doing just fine.

### Source Note

However, if your body resists feeling any sense of safety and your nervous system is very clear that threat is part of your life, investigate whether there is something unsafe in your current reality. Don't try to convince yourself that you are safe, when it isn't actually true. Use this exercise and your awareness to make whatever changes you need to make to safely remove yourself as a target within a dangerous environment. You are here to live your life—not to sacrifice your unique purpose to someone else's misguided pain and control.

reflectionPrompts: When you focus on the physical sensation of your feet connecting to the ground, what shifts in your awareness or emotional state?
As you sit with the phrase 'I am safe. It is safe to be here,' what feelings or inner voices arise in response?
In what ways might you gently acknowledge and soothe any parts of you that carry old messages of fear or trepidation?

Focus on deepening your breath, allowing the inhales to reach your lower abdomen and extending your exhales. Slowly bring your awareness to your feet, feeling their connection to the earth, and gradually scan upward to your pelvic floor. As you rest your attention in this lower part of your body, gently repeat the words 'I am safe. It is safe to be here,' noticing any sensations or feelings that arise with compassion and without judgment.

teachings.title: The Three-Card Body Dialogue Process
teachings.summary: This foundational process introduces a structured way to engage with the Elevate Your Body To Love cards. It offers a gentle, reflective approach to connecting with specific body parts through reading, contemplation, and conscious touch.
teachings.bodyMarkdown:
## Opening

Engaging with your body through structured dialogue offers a profound way to tune into its wisdom. The Three-Card Body Dialogue Process provides a core foundation for working with the *Elevate Your Body To Love* cards. Whether you are seeking life guidance, exploring a specific physical symptom, or simply deepening your connection with your physical form, this process offers a gentle, structured pathway. It can be practiced in solitude or shared within a group, adapting to your current needs while maintaining its core intention of deep listening.

## Core Teaching

The heart of this practice lies in a sequence of three cards: Purpose, Inquiry, and Transcendence. For each step of the journey, the approach remains consistent, creating a safe and predictable rhythm for your body to respond to. 

The process unfolds through five distinct steps for each card. First, you are invited to read the card slowly, speaking the words aloud if possible, allowing the vibration of your voice to interact with the message. Next, you close your eyes and contemplate the message, simply noticing what arises within your inner landscape without judgment. 

The third step brings physical connection: placing your hand on the specific body area being explored and offering words of acknowledgment: "I see you. I hear you. Thank you." This simple act of recognition can be deeply validating for the body. Following this, you write down one thing that stood out to you, anchoring the insight. Only when you feel truly ready do you move to the next card in the sequence.

When you reach the Transcendence card, the practice deepens. You are invited to speak the statement aloud in the first person, as if it is already your lived reality. As you speak the words, pay close attention to how they land within your physical form. If you encounter resistance, there is no need to force past it; simply acknowledge it with gentleness. Then, speak the words again, inviting the very cells of this body part to listen and to begin re-membering this statement as truth.

## What to Notice

As you move through this process, pay attention to the subtle shifts in your physical and emotional state. Notice any areas of tension that arise when reading certain cards, and observe how the simple act of placing your hand on your body affects your breathing and nervous system. When speaking the Transcendence statement, be particularly mindful of any internal voices of doubt or physical sensations of constriction. These are not signs of failure, but rather important pieces of information from your body, asking for the very acknowledgment you are practicing.

## Reflection

This structured dialogue is a practice of building trust with your body. By consistently offering the same gentle sequence of reading, contemplating, touching, and acknowledging, you create a reliable container for exploration. The process asks us to slow down and listen, honoring the body as a source of wisdom rather than an object to be fixed. It reminds us that healing often begins with the simple, profound act of saying, "I see you."

## Practice

Set aside a quiet time to engage with the Three-Card Body Dialogue Process. Choose an area of your body you feel drawn to explore. Follow the five steps for the Purpose and Inquiry cards: read slowly aloud, close your eyes and contemplate, place your hand on the area and say "I see you. I hear you. Thank you," write down one insight, and move forward when ready. When you reach the Transcendence card, speak the statement in the first person, noticing any resistance, and then speak it again, inviting your cells to listen and re-member this truth.

## Source Note

This teaching is drawn from the *Elevate Your Body To Love Booklet*, specifically focusing on the foundational practice outlined for engaging with the cards. The process reflects a commitment to compassionate, embodied listening and the transformative power of acknowledging our physical form.
