teachings.sourceTitle: When Bending Breaks You: The Emotional Roots of Back Pain
teachings.title: When Bending Breaks You: The Emotional Roots of Back Pain
teachings.summary: Susan invites readers to consider chronic back pain not only as a physical problem but as a somatic message shaped by a lifetime of bending to others. The article links nervous-system conditioning and habitual people-pleasing to rigidity and pain in the spine, and offers a gentle, embodied path of boundary-setting, breath, and nervous-system re‑training. Healing is framed as slow, tender re-parenting of the body and choices rather than quick fixes.
teachings.bodyMarkdown:
There are moments when the body speaks a language we cannot ignore. A sudden twinge, a persistent ache, a stiffness that limits our very freedom to move. It’s a profound and intimate communication, a signal from our deepest self that something is out of balance.

And perhaps nothing makes that complexity more exquisitely, undeniably *felt* than a spine that has begun to protest.

A dull ache that blossoms into a hot, searing pain. A stiffness that greets you in the morning and refuses to leave. That sudden, sharp catch that takes your breath away and drops you to your knees. Our backs… they have a way of demanding our full attention, don’t they?

Many of us have encountered people, or have been the person, plagued by debilitating back pain for years. They may have done everything the doctors recommended: physiotherapy, chiropractic adjustments, epidural injections, even considering surgery. Yet nothing provides more than fleeting relief. Often, the body is a portrait of tension, the posture rigid, as if braced for a blow.

There is a common sentiment expressed in these situations: “It feels like I’m made of glass. One wrong move, and I’ll shatter.”

One wrong move. The phrase hangs in the air. As we explore the story, not just of the back, but of the life, a pattern often emerges. A story of a person who has spent a lifetime bending. Bending to the expectations of demanding parents. Bending to the needs of a partner, whose career always came first. Bending to the whims of clients or employers. This is a master of accommodation, a virtuoso of flexibility… until their own body refuses to bend another inch.

## The Sacred Channel of Communication

In the sacred architecture of the body, the spine is everything. It is our central pillar, the axis that allows us to stand upright and meet the world. It is the structural support that houses and protects the delicate spinal cord, that superhighway of information, the central channel of communication between the brain and the rest of our being. It is, in a very real sense, our backbone.

But it’s not just a physical structure. It’s an energetic and emotional one, too. The spine is meant to be a living paradox: exquisitely strong *and* gracefully flexible. It’s designed to hold us steady while allowing for the fluid, dynamic dance of life. When we have a conflict around this paradox in our own lives, the spine often becomes the messenger.

When we feel unsupported in our lives, when we carry burdens that are not ours to bear, the spine can begin to curve under the perceived weight. When we are terrified of making a mistake, of being seen as weak, we can become rigid, our fear calcifying our posture until we lose all fluidity. And when we feel utterly defeated, when we have given up on our own right to stand tall and take up space, the spine can begin to collapse, a physical manifestation of a spirit that has lost its will.

The spine’s screaming truth is one the conscious mind may have refused to acknowledge: that we have bent so far and for so long that we are breaking. The rigidity isn’t a flaw; it was a desperate attempt by the body’s wisdom to create a boundary where our voice had not. It is a primal scream of, “No more.”

## The Courage to Stand Firm

This work is about courage. Not the swashbuckling, heroic kind, but the quiet, internal courage to stand firm in your own truth. The courage to say “no” without apology. The courage to disappoint someone else in order to be true to yourself. For so many, this is terrifying territory. An entire sense of safety and self-worth may have been built on the ability to be accommodating, to be the “easy” one.

“But if I stop bending,” comes the fear-filled question, “won’t I just be… rigid? An unfeeling wall? Won’t everyone leave me?”

Here is a very good thing to know: true strength is never rigid. Think of an old oak tree in a storm. It stands strong not because it is unyielding, but because it has deep roots and the capacity to sway. Its flexibility is an integral part of its strength. Rigidity, on the other hand, is born of fear. It’s the brittleness of a branch that has lost its life force and is destined to snap under pressure.

Our neural pathways get carved by our earliest experiences. If, as children, we learned that our survival depended on accommodating the moods and needs of those around us, our nervous system wires itself for that reality. We become experts at self-abandonment. The neural pathways for “stand my ground” or “speak my truth” remain un-trodden, while the superhighway for “please others at all costs” becomes our default setting. The body, in its infinite intelligence, then reflects this inner state. The tension becomes chronic, the muscles guarding the spine lock down, and the energy in that central channel becomes stagnant.

This isn’t a failing. It’s a survival strategy that has outlived its usefulness. The pain is not a punishment; it is a profound invitation to create a new pattern, to consciously choose a different way of being.

I see this pattern so often. The dutiful daughter who cares for her aging parents, her own dreams deferred, feeling a persistent, grinding ache in her upper back as if carrying them physically. The people-pleasing entrepreneur who says “yes” to every client demand, his lower back screaming in protest at the constant self-betrayal. The spiritual seeker who intellectually understands boundaries but whose body is terrified to enact them, experiencing spasms of pain whenever conflict arises. The body doesn’t lie. It simply reflects the places where our energy is blocked, where our truth is being suppressed. The tension is the telegram. The pain is the plea for a new way of living, a new way of relating to ourselves and the world around us.

[PROMO_SESSIONS]

## Rewiring the Roots of Your Being

For so many, the healing isn’t in another adjustment or injection. It is in the slow, tender practice of learning to feel one’s own ground. It is in the small, radical acts of authenticity. It might start with telling a client, “No, that change isn’t possible at this stage without renegotiating the contract.” The heart may hammer in the chest, but the feared catastrophic consequences often fail to materialize. It can continue with telling a partner, “I need to spend this weekend alone, just for me.” The familiar wave of guilt, the fear of disappointment, may arise. But often, others can and do understand. We begin to see that the catastrophic consequences we fear live mostly in our own minds, echoes of a past that is no longer our present reality.

We can work with the body, not just the mind. We can invite ourselves to simply stand and feel our feet on the floor, to feel the support of the earth rising up to meet us. To imagine the spine not as a fragile column of glass, but as that strong, flexible oak tree, rooted deep in the earth and reaching for the sky. We can use breath to move energy through the spinal column, to gently loosen the grip of those chronically tight muscles.

It isn’t a quick fix. It is a journey of re-parenting the nervous system, of proving to the body, breath by breath, choice by choice, that it is now safe to be authentic. That we can be both strong *and* flexible. That our worth is not tied to our willingness to break ourselves for others.

This is crucial work, and it must be done with exquisite gentleness. There is no forcing, no pushing, no ‘powering through.’ That is the energy that created the pattern in the first place. The healing comes from a different quality of attention altogether. It is the quality of a loving mother tending to a sensitive child. It is the patience of a gardener tending a delicate seedling. We are not fixing a machine; we are coaxing a living system back into its natural state of coherence and flow. It involves listening, deeply listening, to the body’s subtle cues. The sigh of relief when you cancel an obligation you never wanted. The subtle warmth that spreads through your chest when you speak a simple truth. The feeling of groundedness that comes from taking a slow, mindful walk. These are the signposts on the path home to yourself. It is a path of remembering the inherent wisdom that has been there all along, waiting patiently beneath the layers of conditioning and fear.

Consider the profound shift that occurs when this healing takes place. The bracing is gone. A new ease settles in. A genuine smile can finally reach the eyes.

There is a freedom in realizing one can go dancing after years of being afraid the back would ‘go out.’ The fear subsides, and the body simply… dances.

The spine, for so long a source of pain and limitation, can remember its true nature: to be the sacred, central channel for the dance of life.

What is your spine communicating to you? Where in your life are you being asked to find a new relationship between bending and standing firm, between flexibility and integrity? Perhaps you might take a moment to stand, close your eyes, and feel into your own beautiful, wise backbone. Let it speak to you. It has so much wisdom to share.

With infinite love and support on your journey,
Susan

teachings.sourceTitle: The Instruments of Love's Expression: What Your Hands Reveal
teachings.title: The Instruments of Love's Expression: What Your Hands Reveal
teachings.summary: Susan reflects on the hand as a living extension of the heart—both a biological marvel and a tender instrument of connection. She interweaves personal story, nervous‑system science (vagus stimulation and oxytocin), and somatic insight to show how touch, posture, and hand sensations reveal our inner states and offer a path back to ease. The piece invites curiosity about symptoms (coldness, tension, eczema, arthritis) as meaningful signals and offers a short, hands‑centered practice to open toward receptivity and gratitude.
teachings.bodyMarkdown:
A few years ago, my daughter brought her firstborn, a tiny, red-faced, beautiful boy, to my home. I remember the moment she placed him in my arms. He was so new, so fragile, a little bundle of pure potential. As I held him, his miniature hand, a perfect replica of a grown man’s but impossibly small, unfurled and wrapped its fingers around my thumb. And in that simple, instinctual grasp, a universe of connection opened. A current of love, fierce and tender, flowed from my heart, down my arm, and into that tiny, trusting hand.

It’s a complex business, being human. We navigate this world of sensation and emotion, of connection and separation, often forgetting the profound intelligence of the body that carries us. We get so caught up in our thoughts, our plans, our worries… we forget that we are, in our very essence, instruments of love. And nowhere is this more exquisitely expressed than through our hands.

## The Heart’s Ambassadors

Think of your hands. Really, take a moment. Look at them. Turn them over. Notice the intricate map of lines on your palms, the unique whorls of your fingerprints, the shape of your nails. These are not just tools for doing. They are extensions of your heart, your primary ambassadors to the world.

Each hand is a marvel of biological engineering—27 bones, a complex network of muscles, ligaments, and nerves, all working in exquisite coordination. They extend from the heart region, from the energetic center of our being, reaching out to give and to receive. How we literally ‘handle’ life—the way we touch, hold, grasp, create, and connect—is a direct reflection of our relationship with ourselves and with the world. Are our hands open, soft, and receptive? Or are they clenched, tight, and guarded? The body never lies.

When we feel safe and connected, our hands are often warm, relaxed. We might find ourselves gesturing openly, reaching out to punctuate our words, to offer a comforting touch to a friend’s arm. This is the natural state of our nervous system when it is in a parasympathetic, or “rest and digest,” mode. It’s a state of flow, of trust. But when we perceive a threat—whether real or imagined—the body’s ancient survival wiring kicks in. The sympathetic nervous system, our “fight or flight” response, floods our system with stress hormones. Our muscles tense, our heart rate increases, and often, our hands grow cold as blood is shunted to the larger muscles needed for a potential escape. Our hands might clench into fists, a primal posture of defense. We are, in that moment, literally out of touch.

## The Neuroscience of a Loving Touch

This isn’t just poetry; it’s neuroscience. The simple act of gentle, caring touch has a powerful effect on our physiology. When someone we trust holds our hand, strokes our arm, or gives us a hug, it stimulates pressure receptors under the skin called Pacinian corpuscles. These receptors send signals directly to the vagus nerve, a key player in our parasympathetic nervous system.

Stimulating the vagus nerve helps to slow our heart rate, lower our blood pressure, and decrease the production of stress hormones like cortisol. It also triggers the release of oxytocin, often called the “love hormone” or “cuddle chemical.” Oxytocin is the neurochemical basis of bonding and connection. It’s the hormone that floods a mother’s system after childbirth, that surges when we fall in love, that fosters feelings of trust, generosity, and empathy. Every time you offer a gentle hand, you are offering a dose of this powerful, healing neurochemistry.

I remember a time, many years ago, when I was going through a particularly painful separation. I felt adrift, lost in a sea of grief. A dear friend came to sit with me. She didn’t say much. She simply sat beside me on the sofa and took my hand in hers. She didn’t try to fix me or cheer me up. She just held my hand. And in that quiet, simple act of presence, something in me began to soften. The rigid knot of grief in my chest loosened its grip. Her touch was an anchor in the storm, a silent message that I was not alone. Her hand, an instrument of her heart’s compassion, literally helped my nervous system find its way back to a sense of safety.

[PROMO_SESSIONS]

## When the Instruments Are in Distress

Because our hands are such sensitive instruments of connection and expression, they are also one of the first places the body speaks its distress. When we feel anxious about our ability to handle life’s challenges, our hands can become clammy or shaky. If we are being “heavy-handed” in our approach to a situation, trying to force or control an outcome, we might develop tension or pain in our hands and wrists. Arthritis in the hands can reflect a pattern of self-criticism or criticism of others, a rigidity in how we are handling our lives and relationships.

Skin conditions like eczema can be particularly telling. The skin is our boundary, our interface with the world. When it becomes inflamed, itchy, and irritated, it’s often a sign of a deeper irritation, a conflict between our inner world and our outer experience. With the hands, an itching can sometimes point to a deep, unmet desire to *do* something—to create, to reach out, to change a situation we feel stuck in. The body is itching for a different way of handling things. I worked with a woman once, a gifted artist who had put her creative life on hold to raise her family. She developed a painful, persistent case of eczema on her hands. Through our work together, she came to see that her hands were, in a way, grieving. They were itching to hold a paintbrush again, to feel the texture of clay. As she began to carve out small pockets of time for her art, the eczema began to recede. Her hands just wanted to be heard.

It’s so important to approach these symptoms not as enemies to be defeated, but as sacred messengers. The body is not betraying you. It is trying, with its profound and ancient wisdom, to get your attention. It is inviting you into a deeper conversation. What would it be like to meet the pain in your hands with curiosity instead of judgment? To ask it, gently, what it might be trying to communicate? Perhaps the coldness in your hands is a sign that you are feeling disconnected, “out of touch” with yourself or with a loved one. Perhaps the ache is a reflection of a deep-seated belief that you have to “get a grip” and handle everything on your own.

## The Grace of Open Hands

Here is a very good thing to know: handling life beautifully isn’t about control. It’s about balance, sensitivity, and trust. It’s about learning to hold with strength and to let go with grace. It’s about knowing when to act and when to be still. It’s about developing a relationship with life that is more like a dance than a battle.

The ultimate transcendence for the hands is to become instruments of grace. This happens when we release the need to clench, to control, to manage everything. It happens when we learn to open our hands in trust, both in giving and in receiving. An open hand cannot control, but it can receive. It can feel the warmth of the sun, the coolness of a breeze, the texture of a stone, the hand of a beloved. It can receive the gifts the universe is constantly offering, gifts we often miss when our fists are clenched.

There is a beautiful practice you can do. Find a quiet place to sit for a few moments. Close your eyes, and bring your awareness to your hands. Simply notice them. Feel their weight, their temperature. Then, begin to gently massage one hand with the other. Trace the lines on your palm. Gently squeeze each finger, from the base to the tip. As you do, bring a sense of profound gratitude to your hands. Thank them for all they do, for all they have carried, for all they have created. Then, when you are ready, simply rest your hands in your lap, palms facing up. An ancient posture of receptivity. Imagine a soft, warm light pouring into your open palms, filling them with ease, with grace, with love. Sit with that feeling for as long as you like. Notice any sensations, any emotions that arise. This is the beginning of a new conversation.

Your hands have a purpose far beyond the tasks they perform. They are here to build, to create, to soothe, to heal. They are the instruments of your heart’s deepest longing to connect. May you learn to handle your own beautiful, tricky, human life with the utmost tenderness. May you trust the wisdom in your hands, and may they always be a source of love and connection in the world.


---

teachings.title: A Practice for Kidney Healing and Emotional Flow
teachings.summary: Susan frames the kidneys as both literal and symbolic alchemists of emotional balance, inviting readers to cultivate fluidity rather than holding. The tone is compassionate and practical, emphasizing small, consistent attention and neuroplastic change rather than dramatic fixes.
teachings.bodyMarkdown:
Many of us have experienced a subtle, persistent feeling of being stuck. It may not be a grand, dramatic blockage, but a pattern in the small, everyday currents of life. A project stalls. A difficult conversation is postponed. A feeling rises and then gets lodged somewhere in the body—a dull, heavy ache that we try to ignore. It's a feeling of being waterlogged, bogged down by unspoken fears and a sense of overwhelm that can be difficult to name.

It was during a deep meditation that the message came, as they so often do, not in a shout but in a whisper from my own body. The image of two beautiful, bean-shaped organs appeared in my mind’s eye, working tirelessly. My kidneys. And with the image came a question: *What if you could learn to flow like water?*

It’s a tricky business, being human. We are taught to build dams, to control the flow, to hold things in. But our bodies know a different truth. Our bodies are rivers, not reservoirs. And no part of us knows this better than our kidneys, the master alchemists of our internal ocean.

## The Alchemists of Your Inner Ocean

Did you know that your kidneys filter your entire blood supply every 30 minutes? Every single day, these incredible organs process about 200 quarts of fluid, diligently sifting out what is no longer needed and returning the purified essence back to the whole. They are the master chemists of our bodies, maintaining the delicate balance of our internal waters, the very medium of our life force.

In the language of the body as a sacred messenger, the kidneys speak to our capacity for emotional balance and flow. When we are in a state of grace, our emotions—even the difficult ones like fear, grief, and anger—move *through* us. They are processed, filtered, and released, just like the fluids in our bodies. But when we become overwhelmed, when we feel like victims of our circumstances, or when we hold onto fear, these emotions can become stagnant. They crystallize, energetically speaking, creating what can manifest as physical issues. In the Body Cards system, we see kidney stones as the literal crystallization of unprocessed emotions, particularly fear.

Ancient wisdom traditions have long understood this connection. In Chinese Medicine, the kidneys are considered the seat of our foundational life energy, or *Jing*, and are associated with the emotion of fear. A healthy flow of energy in the kidneys gives us willpower, determination, and a sense of deep security. When the energy is depleted or blocked, however, it can manifest as chronic fear, anxiety, and a feeling of being emotionally overwhelmed.

This isn’t about blame or judgment. It’s about compassion and awareness. The patterns that lead to this stagnation are often rooted deep in our past, in neural pathways laid down in childhood when we learned that expressing our full range of emotions was not safe. Perhaps we were told to “stop crying” or that being scared was a sign of weakness. So, we learned to hold it in. We built the dam. And for a time, it served us. It kept us safe. But now, the water is rising, and the dam is beginning to strain.

The beautiful truth is that we can change these patterns. Through the power of neuroplasticity, we can create new neural pathways. We can teach our bodies and our nervous systems a new way of being—a way of flow, release, and trust. We can learn to work *with* our kidneys, consciously, to support their profound work of purification and balance.

[PROMO_SESSIONS]

## A Daily Practice for Kidney Support

How do we begin to support these vital organs and invite emotional flow back into our lives? It begins not with a grand gesture, but with small, consistent acts of conscious attention. Here is a gentle, three-part practice you can begin today. It is a practice of water, visualization, and breath—a way to honor the sacred flow within you.

Find a quiet space where you can be undisturbed for 10-15 minutes. Sit comfortably, with your spine tall but not rigid. Close your eyes and take a few gentle breaths.

### 1. The Water Meditation

Begin by bringing your awareness to the element of water. You might imagine a gentle stream, a flowing river, or the vast, rhythmic ocean. Feel its qualities: its fluidity, its persistence, its ability to cleanse and carry away.

Now, bring a glass of water with you to your practice space. Hold it in your hands. Feel its temperature, its weight. Before you drink, offer a silent blessing to the water. You might say, *“Thank you, water, for your cleansing, healing energy. May you purify my body and my spirit.”*

Take a slow, conscious sip. As you swallow, imagine this blessed water flowing down into your body, a current of pure, liquid light. Visualize it reaching your kidneys, bathing them in this healing energy. Imagine it helping them in their work, effortlessly washing away any energetic debris, any stagnant fear or worry that has accumulated. Feel a sense of gratitude for this simple, profound act of nourishment.

### 2. Emotional Flow Visualization

Now, let your awareness rest on your low back, the area where your kidneys reside. Place your hands there if it feels comforting. Breathe into this space.

Bring to mind a recent situation where you felt a surge of emotion that you might have suppressed—perhaps a flicker of irritation, a wave of sadness, or a pang of fear. Don’t choose your biggest trauma; start with something small, manageable.

Instead of tensing against the feeling, see if you can simply allow it to be there. Now, visualize this emotion as a color, a texture, or a shape within your kidneys. No judgment. Just observation. See it held there.

Now, with each exhale, imagine a gentle stream of clear water flowing through your kidneys, rinsing this colored or textured energy. Visualize the stream carrying the emotional energy down, out of your body, and deep into the earth, where it can be composted and transformed. You are not pushing or forcing; you are simply allowing the natural flow of release. Inhale, a sense of spaciousness. Exhale, a sense of release. Continue this for several minutes, allowing the inner stream to run clear.

### 3. Fear Release Breathwork

Fear has a specific frequency in the body. It often creates a feeling of being frozen or contracted. This final part of the practice uses breath and sound to gently dissolve that contraction.

Still focusing on the area of your kidneys, take a deep breath in. As you exhale, release the breath with an audible, gentle sigh: *“Haaaaaa.”* This is not a forceful sound, but a soft, open-throated release.

As you make the sound, imagine you are vibrating the very cells of your kidneys. The sound is a wave of energy that is gently loosening any hardened, crystallized fear. It’s like a gentle hum that says, *“It is safe to let go. It is safe to flow.”*

Continue for 5-10 breaths. With each sigh, feel the tension in your low back and throughout your body begin to soften, to melt. Feel the frozen places begin to thaw, allowing the river of your life force to flow more freely.

## The Invitation

This practice is an invitation to a new relationship with your body and your emotions. It is a way to become an active participant in your own healing, a conscious partner to the incredible wisdom of your kidneys. You might choose to do this full practice daily, or perhaps just the water meditation in the morning and the fear release breathwork before sleep. The key is consistency and gentle, loving attention.

Your body is not your enemy. Its symptoms are not a punishment. They are messages, whispers from your soul, inviting you to come home to yourself, to your wholeness, to the sacred, flowing river of your own being.


---

## Explore Related Systems

Your body is an interconnected web of wisdom. Each system speaks to and through the others. Continue your exploration:

- [When Holding On Hurts: The Emotional Patterns Behind Bladder Issues](/blog/bladder-emotional-patterns)

**More on Kidneys:**

teachings.title: A Practice for Thyroid Balance and Energetic Harmony
teachings.summary: Susan frames the thyroid as both a biological regulator and an energetic center that holds your authentic rhythm and capacity for expression. She invites a relational approach—listening to the body’s messages rather than trying to ‘fix’ it—and offers simple, accessible practices (throat meditation, rhythm awareness, butterfly tap, healing hum) to support gentle rebalancing through consistent, compassionate attention. The emphasis is on returning to an authentic pace and creating small daily rituals that honor bodily wisdom.
teachings.bodyMarkdown:
There is an ancient wisdom that lives in your body, a knowing that predates language, culture, and even conscious thought.

We are born into a world that seems to have its own frantic, unrelenting pulse. The push to do more, be more, achieve more. The subtle, and sometimes not-so-subtle, messaging that our worth is tied to our productivity. And then there is the other side of the coin—the fear of being too much, too loud, too visible, which can cause us to shrink and slow our own life force until we feel like a ghost in our own lives.

I remember a time, years ago, when my own rhythm was a chaotic symphony of extremes. I was running a busy healing practice, raising my children, and trying to be a perfect partner, friend, and daughter. My days were a blur of frantic activity, fueled by caffeine and sheer willpower. I would collapse into bed at night, my body buzzing with an exhaustion so deep it felt like it had settled in my bones. Then, the pendulum would swing. I would wake up with a leaden feeling, a sense of being underwater, where even the simplest task felt like a monumental effort. My body was screaming at me, but I didn’t yet have the language to understand its desperate messages. It wasn’t until I began a deep, intentional dialogue with my own body, and specifically with the wisdom of my thyroid, that I started to untangle the knots and find my way back to a more authentic, life-giving pace.

## The Butterfly of Transformation

At the base of your throat, nestled like a delicate butterfly, sits the thyroid gland. This is not just a piece of biological machinery, a simple regulator of hormones. It is a center of immense energetic wisdom, a sacred site within the landscape of your body. In many wisdom traditions, this area is known as the throat chakra, the center of communication, truth, and authentic expression. Your thyroid is the physical embodiment of this energetic center. It governs your metabolism, yes—the rate at which you turn the substance of the world into the fire of your own life. But its influence is so much vaster. It is the conductor of your personal rhythm, the keeper of your authentic pace.

When your thyroid is in a state of harmonious balance, you move through the world with a sense of grounded grace. You have the energy to meet the demands and joys of your life, but you are not driven by a frantic, anxious need to prove your worth through doing. You can rest deeply and without guilt, and you can act with clear, focused purpose. You are in tune with the unique, beautiful rhythm that is yours and yours alone. It feels like coming home to yourself.

But what happens when this delicate balance is disturbed? What is the body trying to communicate when the thyroid’s song becomes a cry of distress?

## When the Rhythm is Lost

In my three decades of working with clients, I have seen two primary ways that the thyroid communicates its profound distress: hypothyroidism and hyperthyroidism. From a conventional medical perspective, these are often seen as dysfunctions to be corrected, problems to be managed. I invite you, just for a moment, to consider them from a different point of view—as sacred messages from a body that is doing its absolute best to keep you safe and whole in a world that often feels unsafe and fragmented.

*Hypothyroidism*, or an underactive thyroid, can be understood as the body’s intelligent attempt to slow you down, to pull you inward, to protect you from a world that feels overwhelming or dangerous. It can manifest as persistent fatigue, weight gain, depression, brain fog, and a general sense of sluggishness, as if you’re moving through molasses. So often, this is a deeply embodied response to a core belief that you are “too much.” Perhaps in your childhood, you were told you were too loud, too sensitive, too emotional, too *you*. You learned, on a cellular level, that to be safe and to be loved, you had to dampen your own life force, turn down the volume of your own being. These old survival strategies become deeply ingrained in our neural pathways, and the body, in its infinite wisdom and loyalty, complies by slowing everything down. It is an act of love, a misguided attempt to keep you safe.

*Hyperthyroidism*, or an overactive thyroid, is the other side of the same coin, the other extreme of the same pendulum swing. Here, the body is running on overdrive, flooded with stress hormones, fueled by the deeply ingrained belief that you must constantly be doing, achieving, and accomplishing in order to be worthy of love and belonging. This can lead to heart palpitations, anxiety, insomnia, unexplained weight loss, and a feeling of being constantly on edge, like a car engine that is always redlining. It is as if the body is screaming, “Faster, faster, or you won’t be enough! You’ll be abandoned! You’ll be found lacking!” This, too, is an old pattern, a neural pathway carved in the tender soil of your early life, a strategy that once helped you survive.

Whether you are experiencing the deep, heavy slowness of hypo- or the frantic, buzzing speed of hyper-, the underlying message is the same: you have lost touch with your own authentic rhythm. You are trying to live your life according to a pace that is not your own. But here is the beautiful, hopeful truth: you can come back into balance. You can, with compassion and gentle awareness, begin to create new neural pathways. You can learn to listen to the wisdom of your thyroid and find your way back to a pace that is both sustainable and deeply joyful.

[PROMO_SESSIONS]

## A Practice for Thyroid Balance

This is not about “fixing” your thyroid, but about entering into a loving, respectful, and conscious relationship with this vital center of your being. It is about creating the conditions of safety and presence that allow your body to do what it knows how to do best: heal and return to its natural state of balance. Here is a simple practice that you can begin today.

### Throat Meditation

Find a comfortable place where you can be undisturbed for a few minutes. You can sit or lie down. Close your eyes and bring your awareness to your breath. Don’t try to change it, just notice it. Feel the gentle rise and fall of your chest, the cool air entering your nostrils, the warm air leaving. Now, gently bring your attention to the base of your throat, to the place where your thyroid resides. You may not be able to feel it physically, and that’s perfectly fine. Simply hold your attention in this area with a soft, gentle focus.

Imagine a soft, luminous, sapphire-blue light glowing in this space. This is the light of truth, of peace, of authentic expression. With each inhale, imagine this light growing a little brighter, a little warmer, filling your entire throat area with its healing energy. With each exhale, release any tension, any fear, any old, unspoken words that have been lodged here. Let go of the stories that have kept you from speaking your truth and living in your authentic rhythm. If your mind wanders, gently guide it back to the blue light. Stay with this for five to ten minutes, allowing the gentle blue light to soothe, nourish, and balance your thyroid.

### Rhythm Awareness

This is a practice of bringing mindful awareness into the moments of your day. Begin to notice your own personal rhythm without judgment. Are you rushing to finish an email when you could move more slowly and intentionally? Are you dragging your feet on a project that you feel a genuine spark of excitement about? Simply notice. The act of bringing compassionate awareness to your patterns is the first and most powerful step in changing them.

Throughout the day, you can ask yourself this gentle question: “What is my authentic pace in this moment?” Not the pace that you think you *should* be moving at, or the pace the world demands, but the pace that feels true to your body and your energy level right now. You might be surprised by what you discover. It might be slower than you think. It might be faster. The wisdom is in the listening.

### Energetic Balance Exercises

Here are two simple exercises to help gently stimulate and balance the energy of your thyroid:

1.  **The Butterfly Tap:** Using the fingertips of one hand, gently tap on your collarbones, alternating from side to side. Imagine you are a butterfly gently tapping on a flower. This light, rhythmic tapping helps to stimulate the energy flow in the throat area and awaken the thyroid in a soft, supportive way. Do this for a minute or two while breathing deeply and evenly.

2.  **The Healing Hum:** Humming is a wonderfully simple and profound way to vibrate the throat and bring a sense of calm and balance to the entire nervous system, including the thyroid. You can hum any tune that you like, or simply a single, low note. Close your eyes and feel the gentle vibration in your throat, your chest, and your head. Allow it to be a soothing, internal massage. This tells your body, on a primal level, that you are safe.

## Your Daily Invitation

I invite you to create a small, sacred, daily practice to support your thyroid. It doesn’t have to be long or complicated. The power is in the consistency, the repetition of returning to yourself with love. Perhaps you begin your morning with five minutes of the Throat Meditation, or you practice the Butterfly Tap while you are waiting for your tea to brew. The key is to approach it not as another task to check off your list, but as a radical act of self-love and devotion.

Remember, beloved one, your body is always, always on your side. It is a sacred messenger, a wise and faithful friend, constantly communicating with you, guiding you back to wholeness. By learning to listen to the whispers of your thyroid, you can begin to untangle yourself from the rhythms of fear and expectation, and come back into a beautiful, harmonious, and authentic dance with life.

[PROMO_BODY_CARDS]

With infinite love and support on your journey,
Susan_

teachings.sourceTitle: The Face - The Presentation of Self and the Mirror of Soul
teachings.title: The Face - The Presentation of Self and the Mirror of Soul
teachings.summary: Susan frames the face as an embodied archive — a first language that records how you were seen and how you learned to present yourself. The piece invites a compassionate somatic curiosity toward micro‑expressions, habitual tension, and the identity compromises written on the facial landscape, offering gentle practices (mirror work, hand‑on‑face breathing, short somatic sequences) to relearn safety and expression. The emphasis is on small, nonjudgmental acts of witnessing that gradually reassign the face from performance to radiance.
teachings.bodyMarkdown:
You have always known, in some quiet part of yourself, that the face is more than the sum of eyes nose mouth and skin. It is the first language you learned before words - a living map of how you have been seen and how you have learned to see. It is the interface between the soft mystery of your interior life and the blunt reality of the outside world. In the face you offer a greeting to life and life answers back; your expression becomes the primary bridge between your private landscape and the public sky. When you soften your face you do not merely change an appearance; you alter the flow of energy that moves through you and between you and others.

From the moment of your earliest interactions your face became a field of negotiation. As a child you discovered that certain faces invited warmth and certain faces withheld it. You learned which smile gained attention and which expression was punished. These small recorded experiences became templates - subconscious paradigms that shaped how you present yourself. The face therefore holds a ledger of belonging and exclusion of approval and rejection. It records the rules you learned about when it is safe to show hunger when it is safer to look small when anger must be swallowed. These rules settle not only into your personality but into the muscles of your face the tone of your skin the set of your jaw. Your face is a faithful archivist of survival strategies.

The Face as Messenger

There is a way of listening to the face that is akin to learning a living language. When you look at your own face in a mirror and pay attention without hurry you begin to hear messages. A furrowed brow may speak of years of policing thought. Dryness around the eyes might tell of withheld tears. Tightness in the jaw announces a long history of swallowing truths. Pimples persistent rosacea lines that gather like tributaries across the landscape each carry their own narrative. Rather than medicalize these as simply dysfunctions to be corrected they reveal themselves as meaningful communications from a body that has been doing its best to keep you whole in the only ways it knew how.

The teachings I offer through the card system in Elevate Your Body To Love always begin with this reverent presumption - the body is messenger not adversary. Your face is a concentrated hologram. What it reveals about identity conflicts about the tension between who you truly are and who you believe you must be to belong is astonishingly precise. When you habitually alter your expressions to match expectations you create an internal split. You perform a persona that may secure safety yet drains vitality. The face then becomes a battlefield of energy: one pressure to please and one yearning to be known. Over time the muscles learn to hold a pose and the energy that loves you slowly learns to contract away.

Mask Wearing and the Exhaustion of Performance

There is a kind of fatigue that does not register as tiredness of the limbs but as an exhaustion that lives behind the eyes and along the jawline. The work of mask wearing is slow and resource hungry. To hold a smile when your heart is not smiling to keep your features neutral while your interior is inflamed is to engage in constant micro-effort. Imagine a theatre actor who must maintain a character across years without respite. The performance requires sustained muscular tension micro-regulation of tiny muscles around the eyes cheeks lips that most people never notice. Your nervous system pays for this with upregulated alarm states and lowered vitality. This is one reason TMJ disorders chronic facial tension and chronic facial skin conditions tend to cluster with anxiety and shame: the face becomes a fortress and the cost of keeping it intact is your ease.

You may have learned early that particular faces were rewarded and others punished. So you learned an economy of expression - invest this look to get what you want hide that look to avoid conflict. Over months and years the investments compound. You become hyper-attuned to the gaze of others; you manage your eyebrows your mouth your small smile as if your survival depends upon it. But survival that requires constant performance is not living it is a long form of hiding. The face grows tired because it was never meant to be perpetually curated into an acceptable package. It was meant to breathe to open to laugh and to wrinkle with grief. This endless management freezes aliveness into a mask.

Micro-Expressions - The Body Speaks Truth

There is a curious tenderness in how the face betrays you despite your best efforts at concealment. Micro-expressions are the small involuntary gestures that leak across your features before your conscious strategy can catch them. They are truth seeds. A flicker of worry at the corner of an eye a micro-flinch when someone touches a sore place a subtle tension in the nostrils when anger rises - these are not failures of will but the body’s final allegiance to authenticity. The muscles cannot be fully made to lie forever. The inner truth finds its way out through these tiny unguarded movements. If you learn to attend rather than to punish them you can receive a goldmine of information about what is alive in you what has been defended and what wants to be freed.

Micro-expressions are also the face's wisdom path back to wholeness. They are invitations to notice: when did you first learn to hide this feeling? Who taught you that this expression was dangerous? What would it be like to allow that small movement to fully unfold? The act of witnessing your own involuntary expressions with compassion rather than shame begins a profound recalibration. You cease to be the harsh guard and become a gentle companion who says I see you I am here. In this witnessing the face begins to soften not through effort but through recognition the movement of returning to itself.

Identity Conflicts Written on Skin

When the face bears chronic problems - acne that will not fully clear persistent rashes or early deep lines shaped by worry - they are rarely trivial. They are laden with layers of identity conflict. You may be contorting your face to be acceptable to a set of ideals that are not your own. You may be shrinking yourself to fit into a role - the dutiful child the professional who must never show vulnerability the partner who must always be patient. These compromises ask you to give up parts of your voice in exchange for acceptance. The face then becomes a map of what was surrendered. Often the deepest injuries are reflected not in the theater of dramatic scars but in the quiet constellations of subtle asymmetries and habitual tension patterns.

Seeing this is not an occasion for blame. The strategies you adopted were intelligent in the context of survival. But now you are invited to new intelligence - the capacity to unlearn and to reweave the face with gentler threads. You can begin to reassign the muscles to new purposes: softening not to hide but to open; relaxing not to be small but to be present; smiling not to please but because joy is actually felt. Your face is not broken; it is a script waiting for a new translation.

A Taoist Way of Facing

There is a line in the Tao Te Ching that I carry into this work: "He who knows others is wise; he who knows himself is enlightened." When you look at this through the lens of the face you begin to see that your relationship to others - how you present yourself how you camouflage - is inextricably bound to knowing yourself. The Tao teaches you to return lightness to the body to unmake hypercontrol and let nature reassert its effortless intelligence. "The softest things in the world overcome the hardest things in the world," says the Tao. So learn to counter the hardness of performance with the soft practice of presence. Allow gravity to soften the jaw let the eyes be moistened by compassion let the skin breathe. Underneath the conditioned grammar of your face there is an ancient pliability waiting to be remembered.

Listening Practices for the Face

There are practices that do not require you to fix anything immediately but rather to enter a slow conversation with your face. Begin by placing both hands lightly on your cheeks and feel the warmth of your touch. Breathe and imagine your breath moving into the tissues under your fingers. Let the bones soften beneath your hands. Stay with whatever wants your attention. If a memory arises do not push it away; simply notice and let the face be the courier. Say gently aloud: I see you I hear you thank you. Speak as if the facial muscles are a living child who needs to be reassured. You are not trying to alter appearance you are trying to teach the muscles that safety is possible and expression is welcome.

Another practice is the mirror conversation for five minutes daily. Look into your own eyes and speak to the face as if it were a beloved friend. Ask the simple questions you might have asked a guardian who lived in your earliest years: When did you first learn to do this? What did you give up to hold this look? When did you stop allowing yourself to cry to laugh to frown? Listen patiently for the slightest twitch or softening; these micro-movements are the language of truth. Do not judge let whatever comes be honored. You are creating a new memory in which the face is safe to be itself.

From Mask to Radiance

The deepest reclamation is not merely cosmetic. It is the alchemical shift from shielding to radiance. When you stop trying to manage how others read you your face will begin to reveal what has been there all along - the luminous presence of sheer love. This is not a sentimental phrase but a somatic reality. Love as a state of being has qualities: it warms the skin, it relaxes the jaw it steadies the breath. You can feel that simple radiance when you allow the face to be an honest transmitter of your inner life rather than a curated object for safety. It is the difference between wearing a decorative mask and letting your visage shine from the inside like a lantern.

There will be moments when the old reflexes return and you slip into a practiced expression. When this happens do not scold yourself. Return to your breath and to a practice of naming. Name the habit with kindness and then bring the face back to rest. This is the gentle work of rewiring neural tracks - not with force but with persistent tiny acts of compassion. The neurological pathways that once learned to constrict will slowly learn to expand. The face learns new choreography when you repeatedly give it permission to be real.

A Threefold Inquiry for Your Face

If you are familiar with the three-card process from the cards in Elevate Your Body To Love you can apply the same structure to the face. First, meet your face as Purpose. Recognize its role in your survival how it protected you how it gained you what you needed. Sit with gratitude for the ingenuity of the muscles that learned to hide your pain so you could remain in relationship. Then move into Inquiry. Ask the face what it has been carrying. Invite specific memories to come up and listen for the emotions that arise in the tissues above the bone. Notice the physical sensations and the micro-expressions that appear as you ask. Let your curiosity be courageous but kind. Finally, turn toward Transcendence. Speak aloud a new statement of possibility for your face. It may be as simple as: I allow my face to speak my truth. I welcome tears as evidence of courage. I release the mask that was given to keep me safe and I accept the radiance of love that is mine to show. Repeat the words until your tissues remember them.

Practical Softening - A Short Somatic Sequence

When you notice facial tension begin a short ritual of release. Sit upright place your tongue gently on the roof of your mouth and allow your shoulders to drop. Breathe slowly down into the belly and on the exhale let the jaw unclench as if a tiny sigh passes through the mouth. Soften the eyelids as if a curtain draws over the windows of your face. Keep your hands on your face favoring places that feel tense and send your breath there. Imagine the breath as a river that washes the tightness into a larger ocean of acceptance. Stay with this for several breath cycles returning to it throughout your day. Over time the muscles will come to expect some ease and the face will remember its primary purpose - not to defend but to express the fullness of you.

Becoming the Radiant Face of Love

At the end of the day the task is not to achieve a kind of perfected beauty but to befriend the truth under the mask and allow something deeper to shine. There is a luminous quality that belongs to you when your internal life and your external presentation are aligned. It is the peace that comes when you stop negotiating the terms of your presence with the world and instead stand in the gentle sovereignty of your being. This radiance will alter how people recognize you not because it conforms to an ideal but because it emanates integrity. Your face will not only mirror your soul - it will become an instrument through which your soul meets the world.

He who knows himself is enlightened. Let the Tao’s soft wisdom guide you back to your face. Do not harden into the performance. Allow the muscles to remember the ease of natural expression. Let micro-expressions become teachers rather than secrets. In the slow unfolding of this intimacy you will discover that beneath the conditioned surface you are not a collection of defenses but a field of luminous presence. You are the radiance of sheer love made manifest. Each time you choose to unmask with tenderness you invite the world to breathe with you and together you remember what it meant to belong simply by being. I will walk with you in this remembering as you let your face become the mirror of your soul.
keyThemes: The face as an embodied messenger and archive of survival
Mask‑wearing, performance fatigue, and the nervous system cost
Micro‑expressions as truthful signals and pathways to healing
Identity conflicts and habitual facial patterns
Compassionate witnessing and nonjudgmental inquiry
Simple somatic practices to soften facial tension
Taoist emphasis on softness, ease, and natural expression
Reclaiming authentic radiance rather than cosmetic perfection
reflectionPrompts: Recall an early memory of when you learned to change your face to get attention or avoid trouble — what expression did you adopt, and what did it gain or cost you?
Observe your face now (in a mirror or briefly with closed eyes): what habitual expression do you notice most often, and what do you imagine it is protecting you from?

Pay attention to a recent micro‑expression (a fleeting twitch, flinch, or softening). What feeling or memory seems to be connected to that small movement, and how might you meet it with curiosity rather than criticism?

This is a companioning practice, not medical treatment — consult a health professional for persistent pain, TMJ issues, or skin conditions.

If the material brings up intense distress or trauma memories, consider reaching out to a trauma‑informed therapist, counselor, or trusted support person for guidance and grounding.

teachings.sourceTitle: The Thread That Connects Everything: Living as a Unified Field
teachings.title: The Thread That Connects Everything: Living as a Unified Field
teachings.summary: Susan invites readers to experience their inner life as a single, interconnected field — a luminous thread that weaves together thoughts, emotions, body sensations, relationships, and spirit. Through embodied attention and curiosity, difficult sensations and emotions become messengers rather than enemies, guiding us toward integration and greater wholeness. The piece bridges ancient wisdom (the Tao) and contemporary neuroscience to offer a practical path of moment-to-moment return to presence.
teachings.bodyMarkdown:
It’s a curious thing, this human experience. We spend so much of our lives feeling fragmented, pulled in a thousand different directions. The mind races with yesterday’s regrets and tomorrow’s anxieties. The body aches with tensions we can’t name. Our relationships feel like a complex dance of connection and disconnection. And our deepest spiritual longings… they often feel like a distant echo, a whisper from another world entirely. But what if I told you there is a thread that runs through it all? A luminous, golden cord that weaves through your thoughts, your emotions, your body, your relationships, and your most sacred sense of self. When you learn to feel this thread, you discover that nothing in your experience is separate. It is all one unified field of being. This isn’t just a poetic idea, beloved one. It’s a lived reality, a truth our bodies know even when our minds forget. ## The Symphony of Self Think of your being as a grand symphony. Your thoughts are the woodwinds, sometimes clear and bright, other times melancholic and low. Your emotions are the strings, soaring with joy, trembling with sorrow, vibrating with the full spectrum of feeling. Your body is the percussion, the steady, grounding rhythm that holds it all together. And your spirit? Your spirit is the conductor, the silent presence that guides the entire orchestra into a coherent whole. For most of us, the orchestra is playing out of tune. The woodwinds are in a frantic argument with the strings, and the percussion has lost its rhythm. We experience this as anxiety, as chronic pain, as a sense of being fundamentally at odds with ourselves. We try to fix the individual pieces—we try to “think positive,” to suppress our anger, to numb our physical discomfort. But we’re missing the point. Healing doesn’t come from fixing the individual instruments. It comes from attuning to the conductor, to the unifying thread that runs through the entire symphony. It comes from recognizing that every note, every feeling, every sensation is part of the same beautiful, complex piece of music. I remember a client I worked with years ago, a woman who came to me with debilitating migraines. She had tried everything—medication, dietary changes, every specialist she could find. She saw her migraines as an enemy, a cruel intruder that shattered her life. We began our work not by trying to “get rid of” the pain, but by listening to it. I asked her to close her eyes, to breathe into the sensation, to follow its thread. Where did it live in her body? What was its texture, its color, its temperature? What did it have to say? Slowly, painstakingly, she began to follow the thread. The searing pain in her temples, she discovered, was connected to a deep, unexpressed grief over the loss of her mother. The grief was connected to a lifetime of feeling like she had to be the strong one, the one who never cried. The thread led her back to her own heart, to a place of profound tenderness and vulnerability she had walled off for decades. As she learned to be with her grief, to allow the tears to flow, the migraines began to soften. They didn’t vanish overnight, but they were no longer the enemy. They were a messenger, a guide, a thread leading her back to the wholeness of her own being. ## The Web of Your Being This is the essence of what ancient wisdom traditions have always known, and what modern neuroscience is now beginning to confirm. Our brains are not isolated command centers, but vast, interconnected networks. The field of interpersonal neurobiology, pioneered by Dr. Dan Siegel, speaks of the mind as a relational and embodied process that regulates the flow of energy and information. The key word here is *flow*. When the flow is blocked—by trauma, by suppressed emotion, by rigid beliefs—we experience dis-ease. When the flow is restored, we experience integration, a sense of wholeness and well-being. The Tao Te Ching speaks of this in its own beautiful, poetic language. It describes the Tao as the unnamable, unknowable source from which all things arise and to which all things return. It is the "thread that strings it all together." Chapter 14 says: > Look, it cannot be seen - it is beyond form. > Listen, it cannot be heard - it is beyond sound. > Grasp, it cannot be held - it is intangible. > These three are indefinable; therefore they are joined as one. This "one" is the unified field of your being. It is the silent awareness that holds your thoughts, the compassionate space that holds your feelings, the vibrant aliveness that animates your body. You cannot grasp it with the mind, but you can feel it. You can sense it. You can learn to live from this place of deep, abiding connection. ## Living the Thread So how do we begin to feel this thread in our own lives? It begins with the body. The body is the gateway, the living anchor in the present moment. It is the place where the symphony of the self is most palpable. Start by simply noticing. As you read these words, can you feel the weight of your body in your chair? Can you feel the gentle rise and fall of your breath? Can you sense the subtle hum of energy in your hands, your feet, your heart? Don’t try to change anything. Just notice. This simple act of noticing is an act of profound love. It is a way of saying to your body, "I am here with you. I am listening." From this place of embodied presence, you can begin to follow the threads. When a difficult emotion arises—anxiety, anger, sadness—instead of pushing it away, can you get curious about it? Where do you feel it in your body? Is it a tightness in your chest? A knot in your stomach? A lump in your throat? Breathe with it. Be with it. Let it be what it is. You are not the emotion. You are the loving awareness that holds the emotion. When a racing thought takes hold, can you notice it without getting swept away by it? See it for what it is—a transient electrical impulse in your brain. You are not your thoughts. You are the vast, silent sky through which the clouds of thought pass. This is not a one-time fix. It is a practice, a moment-by-moment returning to the truth of your own being. It is the practice of living as a unified field. Some days, the symphony will feel harmonious and clear. Other days, it will feel dissonant and chaotic. The practice is to be with it all, to hold it all in the loving embrace of your own awareness. This is the journey of a lifetime, my friend. It is the journey of coming home to yourself. It is the journey of discovering that you were never broken, never fragmented. You were always whole, always complete, always connected by that luminous, golden thread.

keyThemes: Embodied awareness as the gateway to integration
Emotions and physical sensations as meaningful messengers
The mind–body–spirit unified field
The practice of noticing and nonreactive curiosity
Ancient wisdom (Tao) connected to modern neuroscience
Grief, vulnerability, and emotional release as healing paths
Moving from fixing parts to attuning to the whole

reflectionPrompts: Recall a recent moment of physical discomfort, tension, or strong emotion. Where did it show up in your body? Describe its qualities (shape, temperature, texture) and what, if anything, that sensation seems to be pointing toward.

When you imagine your inner life as an orchestra, which ‘instrument’ feels out of tune right now (thoughts, emotions, body, relationships, spirit)? What would it take to listen to the conductor — the unifying awareness — for five minutes each day?

Think of a time when a symptom or strong feeling shifted after you attended to it with kindness. What changed in your relationship to that experience, and what small, repeating practice could support more of that shift?
teachings.practiceInvitation: Find a comfortable seated position for 5–7 minutes. Close your eyes if that feels safe, bring attention to the weight of your body on the chair or floor, and take three slow breaths. Gently scan from feet to head, pausing where you notice sensation: note its location and qualities (temperature, density, tone) without trying to change it. If a thought or story arises, simply label it (“thinking”) and return to sensing. If the sensation invites curiosity, breathe toward it for a few cycles and allow whatever wants to move to move. Stop at any time if you feel overwhelmed. This practice is complementary to medical or therapeutic care — consult your healthcare provider for persistent or severe symptoms.
sensitiveContentNotes: This article includes references to grief and chronic pain (migraines) and explores emotional release; these topics can bring up strong feelings.
If you have a history of trauma, recent loss, or intense emotional distress, you may want to pause or practice with additional support from a trusted therapist, clinician, or support person.

The embodied practice offered is gentle and optional. If bodily symptoms are severe or persistent, please consult a medical professional; this content is not a substitute for medical or psychiatric care.

teachings.sourceTitle: Breaking the Spell: How to Recognize and Release Inherited Beliefs
teachings.title: Breaking the Spell: How to Recognize and Release Inherited Beliefs
teachings.summary: Susan invites readers to see many of their core assumptions as handed-down maps — inherited beliefs that quietly shape choices and limit longing. She describes how these beliefs lodge in the body and nervous system and offers gentle, stepwise practices—curious inquiry, body-listening, and small experiments—to recognize and begin releasing those old stories so you can author a new one.
teachings.bodyMarkdown:
It’s a curious thing, this human experience. We arrive, blinking in the light, into a world already in motion, a story already being told. We spend our first years learning the language, the rules, the rhythms of the particular tribe we’re born into. And somewhere along the way, without ever consciously choosing, we absorb their beliefs as our own. They become the invisible architecture of our reality, the water we swim in. We don’t question if the water is wet; it simply *is*. These inherited beliefs—these silent agreements we made before we could even speak—are like spells cast upon us. Not with malicious intent, not always, but with the quiet, insistent power of generations. *This is how the world works. This is what you are capable of. This is what is safe. This is what is forbidden.* They are the legacy of our ancestors’ joys, their sorrows, their fears, and their triumphs. And they live in us, shaping our choices, whispering in our ear, and often, holding us back from the life that is truly ours to live. ## The Unseen Inheritance Think of it like this: you are handed a map at birth. A beautiful, worn, hand-drawn map, filled with familiar landmarks and well-trodden paths. This map was drawn by your parents, and their parents before them. It shows you where to go, what to avoid, where the treasure is buried. For a time, this map is incredibly useful. It keeps you safe. It helps you navigate the known world. But one day, you look up from the map and see a landscape it doesn’t describe. A shimmering mountain range in the distance, a path winding into a forest that the map labels as “dragons.” And a deep, quiet knowing rises within you—a longing to explore *that*. But the map says no. The map says it’s dangerous. The map says you’ll get lost. The spell of the map is strong. It feels like truth. It feels like love, even, the love of those who wanted to protect you. So many of the beliefs that shape our lives were never ours to begin with. They were inherited, absorbed from our families, our cultures, our earliest experiences. Recognizing these inherited spells is the first step toward freedom. It’s the moment you realize you can draw your own map. ## A Story of My Own I remember a client I worked with years ago, a brilliant artist with a heart of gold. She created the most breathtaking paintings, vibrant and alive with a spirit that was uniquely hers. Yet, she could never bring herself to sell them. She’d sabotage every opportunity, miss every deadline, find a reason to pull back at the last moment. She came to me, distraught, believing she was simply a "procrastinator," lazy and undisciplined. As we worked together, a memory surfaced. She was a little girl, no older than five, painting with joyous abandon at the kitchen table. Her father, a man who had struggled financially his whole life, walked in. He looked at her creation, and with a heavy sigh, said, “It’s a lovely hobby, sweetheart. But you can’t make a living as an artist. It’s a fool’s dream.” He wasn’t being cruel. He was trying to protect her from the disappointment he had known. He was casting a spell of safety. But that spell became her reality. *Art is a hobby. You can’t make a living from it. It’s a fool’s dream.* This belief, inherited in a moment of love and fear, had been running her life for decades, a silent, powerful undercurrent. It was the "dragon" on her map. ## The Body Remembers These beliefs aren’t just abstract ideas floating in our minds. They are encoded in our bodies, in our very nervous systems. When that little girl heard her father’s words, her body likely responded. A tightening in her chest, a knot in her stomach, a subtle bracing for disappointment. The body, in its infinite wisdom, remembers. It stores the emotional charge of these experiences, creating a physiological pattern that gets triggered every time a similar situation arises. This is where the insights of neuroscience become so illuminating. Our brains are wired for survival, and they create neural pathways based on our repeated experiences and the emotional weight they carry. An inherited belief, reinforced over years, becomes a well-worn neural superhighway. The thought “I can’t make a living from my art” triggers a cascade of stress hormones, a physiological state of fear and contraction, making it feel viscerally, physically true. It’s not a failure of willpower; it’s a deeply ingrained biological response. The beautiful, hopeful truth, however, is neuroplasticity. The brain can and does change. The body can and does release old patterns. By bringing gentle, compassionate awareness to these bodily sensations, we can begin to unwind the spell. We can create new neural pathways. We can teach our nervous system that it is safe to explore beyond the edges of the old map. ## How to Recognize the Spells So how do we begin to see the invisible? How do we recognize the spells we are living under? It begins with a gentle, curious inquiry. * **Look for the recurring patterns.** Where in your life do you feel stuck? What situations or themes seem to repeat, no matter how hard you try to change them? This is often the signature of an inherited belief at play. * **Listen to your language.** Pay attention to the absolute statements you make about yourself and the world. “I’m just not a creative person.” “You can’t trust anyone.” “Money is always a struggle.” These are often the echoes of inherited beliefs. * **Feel into your body.** When you think about a particular goal or dream, what happens in your body? Is there an openness, an expansion? Or is there a subtle (or not-so-subtle) contraction, a tightness, a feeling of dread? Your body is a powerful truth-teller. It will show you where the spells reside. > Take a moment, beloved one. Think of an area in your life where you feel limited. A dream you’ve held but never pursued. A desire that feels just out of reach. Whisper it to yourself. And then, listen. Listen not with your mind, but with your whole body. What sensations arise? What is the story your body is telling you? This is the beginning of the conversation. This is the first step to breaking the spell. ## Releasing the Inheritance Breaking the spell is not a battle. It is not about declaring war on your past or your family. It is a process of profound compassion and gentle release. It is about honoring the love and protection that may have been at the root of the belief, while also recognizing that it no longer serves you. It’s about seeing the belief for what it is: a story. And you, dear one, are the author of your own life. You can choose to write a new one. This process can be as simple and as profound as placing a hand on your heart when the old belief arises, and whispering, “Thank you. I see you. I know you were trying to keep me safe. But I am safe now. And I am choosing a new way.” It’s about consciously, deliberately choosing thoughts, actions, and experiences that align with the new story you want to live. For my client, it meant starting small. She began by showing one painting to a trusted friend. Then she entered a small local art show. With each step, she was creating a new neural pathway, a new experience in her body that said, *It is safe to share my art. My art has value.* She was teaching her nervous system a new reality, one gentle step at a time. This is the work of a lifetime. It is a journey of returning, over and over again, to the truth of who you are beneath the layers of inherited stories. It is the most courageous, most rewarding journey you will ever take.
